Script.name: 00_util
Script.script:
--[[ aardkit core utils Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31 Shared helpers for the ported MUSHclient plugins. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.version = "1.0.0"
local U = {} aardkit.util = U
--- -- paths ---
-- everything we persist lives under <profile>/aardkit/ -- -- lfs.mkdir returns nil plus a message when it can't - a read-only profile, no -- permission - and we used to throw that away. Every save after it then failed -- too, and with U.save's old fail-open that was two silent failures stacked: -- nothing persisted all session and nothing said so. Say it once. local dirwarned = false
function U.datadir() local d = getMudletHomeDir() .. "/aardkit" if not io.exists(d) then local ok, err = lfs.mkdir(d) if not ok and not io.exists(d) and not dirwarned then dirwarned = true U.err("can't create " .. d .. " (" .. tostring(err) .. ") - nothing will be saved this session") end end return d end
function U.datafile(name) return U.datadir() .. "/" .. name end
--- -- persistence — one table per key, saved as a Lua chunk -- -- Yes, these execute. Mudlet's table.load is dofile() under the hood -- (mudlet-lua/Other.lua), so <profile>/aardkit/<key>.lua is run, not parsed. A -- review raised it and it is a real mechanism, so here is why it stays: -- -- * writing a state file already requires write access to the profile -- directory. Anything with that can edit the plugin scripts sitting beside -- them, or the profile XML Mudlet loads at startup, both of which run too. -- dofile grants an attacker nothing they don't already have. -- * the trust boundary that matters is FOREIGN data, and it's elsewhere and -- already correct. Nothing outside this directory ever reaches table.load: -- migrate reads MUSHclient dumps and loot reads shared pool files, and both -- go through yajl.to_value, which parses as data and cannot execute. -- -- What would change the answer: a state file arriving from anywhere but this -- machine - synced between profiles, downloaded, pasted in by someone helping -- you debug. If that ever becomes a feature, this has to become JSON first. -- Don't quietly widen who can write here. ---
-- Two things were wrong here. table.save does NOT error when it can't open the -- file - it returns nil plus a message (mudlet-lua/Other.lua) - so pcall's ok -- flag said "didn't crash", not "wrote", and a read-only profile reported -- success while the settings went nowhere. -- -- And it wrote in place: table.save opens the target with "w", truncating -- first and writing after, so a crash or a full disk mid-write left a -- half-file - and a half-file won't parse, so the next load fell back to code -- defaults and the lot was gone. Write beside it and rename over, which is -- atomic on one filesystem: the old file stands until the new one is whole. function U.save(key, tbl) local path = U.datafile(key .. ".lua") local tmp = path .. ".new"
-- three outcomes: it raised (ok false, a is the error), it returned nil plus -- a message (ok true, b is the message), or it returned nothing and wrote. local ok, a, b = pcall(table.save, tmp, tbl) local why = (not ok and a) or b if not why and not io.exists(tmp) then why = "wrote nothing" end if why then os.remove(tmp) aardkit.util.err("save " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(why)) return false end
local moved, rerr = os.rename(tmp, path) if not moved then os.remove(tmp) aardkit.util.err("save " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(rerr)) return false end return true end
-- Defaults are a floor, not a fallback: whatever loads gets laid over them, so a -- truncated or half-written state file costs you the saved values, not the keys. -- Without this a bad file returns an empty table and the first plugin that does -- arithmetic on a config field dies at load time and takes itself out. -- -- The floor goes all the way down. It used to stop at the top level, so a nested -- default was replaced wholesale rather than filled in: once anything had saved -- 40_stock's { off = { ["runto rt"] = true } }, adding a second entry to that -- table in code did nothing for anyone who already had a state file, because -- their saved `off` overwrote the whole default including the new key. -- -- Arrays are a deliberate exception. Merging a saved 3-item list over a 5-item -- default leaves items 4 and 5 showing through, which is never what a list -- means - if you removed two entries you want them gone. local function layer(base, over) for k, v in pairs(over) do if type(v) == "table" and type(base[k]) == "table" and #v == 0 and #base[k] == 0 then layer(base[k], v) else base[k] = v end end return base end
local function clone(t) local out = {} for k, v in pairs(t or {}) do out[k] = (type(v) == "table") and clone(v) or v end return out end
function U.load(key, default) local out = clone(default)
local path = U.datafile(key .. ".lua") if not io.exists(path) then return out end
local t = {} if not pcall(table.load, path, t) then U.warn("couldn't read " .. key .. ".lua - using defaults") return out end return layer(out, t) end
-- Geyser hands geometry back as either a number or a "420px" string depending -- on which accessor you reach for, so every panel that lays itself out by hand -- needs this. snd/ui.lua and recallmanager both had their own identical copy. function U.px(v) return tonumber((tostring(v or "0"):gsub("px", ""))) or 0 end
-- Aardwolf prefixes transient status flags onto a mob's short description - -- "(flying) (hidden) a casanova". Anything keying on the name has to take them -- off first, so this lives here rather than in whichever module needed it -- first: S&D and SolaoBot had byte-identical copies and ship separately. function U.strip_flags(m) local s = tostring(m or "") while true do local n = s:gsub("^%s*%b()%s*", "", 1) if n == s then break end s = n end return U.trim(s) end
-- Aardwolf's own commands take the article literally. 'where a kobold guard' -- answers "There is no a kobold guard around here." while 'where kobold guard' -- finds it, and the same goes for hunt and for matching against anything we -- stored under the name without one. Nothing that feeds a mob name to the MUD -- or to a lookup wants the leading article. -- -- 'An?' has to keep the %s+ or it eats the front of "Ancient dragon". function U.strip_art(m) return (tostring(m or ""):gsub("^%s*[Tt]he%s+", ""):gsub("^%s*[Aa]n?%s+", "")) end
--- -- cross-module suggestions -- -- Every module stands alone. Nothing here requires anything else, and a missing -- sibling is never an error - it's a different, usually more manual, path. -- -- But saying "do this by hand" and stopping there is only half an answer. The -- useful sentence is the one naming the thing that would have done it for you, -- said once, at the moment you're being asked to do the work - not at load, and -- never as a nag on a timer. -- -- Private modules are deliberately absent from this table. Pointing someone at -- a repository they can't clone is worse than saying nothing. ---
local REPO = "https://github.com/SeanStoves/aardkit"
local MODULES = { loot = { "Loot Tracker", "Loot%20Tracker" }, snd = { "Search and Destroy", "Search%20and%20Destroy" }, mapper = { "Mapper", "Mapper" }, pt = { "Player Tracker", "Player%20Tracker" }, recall = { "Recall Manager", "Recall%20Manager" }, consider = { "Consider", "Consider" }, spellup = { "Spellups", "Spellups" }, coords = { "Coordinates", "Coordinates" }, statmon = { "Stat Monitor", "Stat%20Monitor" }, mapexporter = { "MapExporter", "MapExporter" }, helpwin = { "Help Window", "Help%20Window" }, goals = { "Goals", "Goals" }, }
-- Is it actually loaded? The namespace existing is the test, because that's -- what every caller then goes on to use. function U.have(key) local ns = aardkit[key] return type(ns) == "table" and next(ns) ~= nil end
-- "You can do X by hand. <Module> does it for you: <link>" -- -- Silent when the module IS loaded, so a caller can put this after its fallback -- without checking twice, and silent for anything not in the table. function U.suggest(key, said) if U.have(key) then return end local m = MODULES[key] if not m then return end local url = REPO .. "/tree/main/" .. m[2] U.out("\n <#8a93a8>" .. (said or "") .. (said and " " or "") .. m[1] .. " does this for you:<r>") U.outLink(" <#3ad07a>" .. url .. "<r>", function() if U.has("openUrl") then openUrl(url) end end, "Open " .. url) echo("\n") end
--- -- gagging -- -- One choke point, so it's greppable and so the ownership rule has somewhere to -- live: a line belongs to whoever gags it first, and nobody should be arming a -- catch-all that overlaps someone else's marker. -- -- This deliberately does NOT try to detect a double-gag by line number. That -- was tried and it is worse than the problem: deleteLine() shifts every later -- line up, so the line AFTER a gagged one reports the same number, and an empty -- {roomchars} block - open and close adjacent, nothing between - had its close -- refused and leaked to the screen. Overlap gets solved where it happens, by -- not matching what someone else owns. ---
-- What we hide from the screen can still be kept in the log. Mudlet's -- appendLog() writes to the logfile without displaying, so a gagged line goes -- to the file behind a marker and the screen never sees it. That makes a -- session log a record of what the MUD sent rather than a record of what we -- chose to let through - which matters when the thing you need to look up -- afterwards is exactly the thing a gag ate. -- -- The signature isn't greppable: the binary documents one argument, "text to -- append to logfile", but Mudlet's console functions conventionally take an -- optional window name first. Try the windowed form, fall back to the bare one. -- Guessing wrong on a Lua-side API is how dechoLink stayed quiet for a -- fortnight. local GCFG = U.load("gaglog", { on = true, mark = "GAGGED -- " })
function U.gaglog(v) if v ~= nil then GCFG.on = v and true or false; U.save("gaglog", GCFG) end return GCFG.on end
function U.gag() if GCFG.on and U.has("appendLog") then local line = getCurrentLine() if line and line ~= "" then local text = (GCFG.mark or "") .. line -- appendLog takes the TEXT, not a window name. It was being called -- as appendLog("main", text), which logged the literal string -- "main" for every gagged line and dropped the line itself - 52 of -- them in a one-minute session, and "GAGGED --" appears in no log -- ever written. The two-arg call succeeded, so the fallback below -- it never ran and nothing ever looked wrong on screen. pcall(appendLog, text) end end deleteLine() return true end
--- -- db -- -- Mudlet's db:update is db:update(sheet, tbl) and nothing else. It finds the row -- from tbl._row_id and asserts if that's missing (mudlet-lua/DB.lua:1411). There -- is no (sheet, fields, query) form - db:set is the by-query one and it writes a -- single column. Every call site here passed a third argument that was silently -- ignored while the row was picked by an _row_id that wasn't there, so the -- assert fired and the write never happened. -- -- All of them already had the fetched row to hand, so: pass it, and let this -- carry the id across. ---
function U.dbupdate(sheet, row, fields) if not (sheet and type(row) == "table" and row._row_id) then U.err("db update: no _row_id - fetch the row first") return false end local t = { _row_id = row._row_id } for k, v in pairs(fields or {}) do t[k] = v end local ok, err = pcall(db.update, db, sheet, t) if not ok then U.err("db update: " .. tostring(err)); return false end return true end
--- -- output -- -- Everything we print uses <#rrggbb> tags, which is NOT a syntax any Mudlet echo -- accepts: cecho wants colour *names*, hecho wants #rrggbb, decho wants <r,g,b>. -- Feed cecho a <#rrggbb> and it quietly drops it, which is how the whole thing -- came out plain. So convert to decho: it's bracket-delimited, so a '#' or a -- comma sitting in the message text can't be mistaken for markup the way it can -- with hecho. ---
local function to_decho(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("<#(%x%x%x%x%x%x)>", function(h) return string.format("<%d,%d,%d>", tonumber(h:sub(1, 2), 16), tonumber(h:sub(3, 4), 16), tonumber(h:sub(5, 6), 16)) end)) end
U.to_decho = to_decho
-- main window function U.out(s) decho(to_decho(s)) end
-- a named console / miniwindow function U.outw(win, s) decho(win, to_decho(s)) end
--- -- compat -- -- Mudlet's C++ API is greppable in the binary; its Lua-side API (Geyser, db, -- LuaGlobal) is compressed into a Qt resource and is not. So anything below that -- lives on the Lua side gets checked at runtime instead of assumed — guessing -- wrong there is how 'clearMap' shipped as a nil call. ---
function U.has(name) return type(_G[name]) == "function" end
--- -- links -- -- dechoLink is the right one: it takes <r,g,b>, which is what to_decho already -- produces. cechoLink was tried and is wrong - it only knows colour names, so -- our <#3ad07a> printed literally. -- -- What was actually broken is the command. Mudlet's own code passes a function -- (mudlet-lua/GUIUtils.lua, cechoLink -> xEcho -> echoLink), and a function is -- unambiguous where a string is Lua to be eval'd at click time, with the -- quoting left to every call site - a mob called Doctor Cameroon "Rusty" Baboon -- is the sort of thing that goes wrong there. Strings still work, they get -- wrapped. -- -- The trailing boolean is useCurrentFormat and xEcho does accept it: four args -- with a boolean fourth is the documented no-window form. -- -- A string cmd gets compiled and run when the link is clicked, so anything -- built from MUD text has to go through %q (which escapes it into a safe Lua -- literal) or be a number. Every call site does today. A function sidesteps the -- question entirely and is the better habit. ---
local function asfunc(cmd) if type(cmd) == "function" then return cmd end local s = tostring(cmd or "") local compile = loadstring or load return function() local fn = compile(s) if fn then fn() end end end
local function plain(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("<[^>]*>", "")) end
function U.outLink(s, cmd, hint) local fn = asfunc(cmd) if U.has("dechoLink") and pcall(dechoLink, to_decho(s), fn, hint or "", true) then return end if U.has("echoLink") then echoLink(plain(s), fn, hint or "", true) return end U.out(s) end
function U.outLinkw(win, s, cmd, hint) local fn = asfunc(cmd) if U.has("dechoLink") and pcall(dechoLink, win, to_decho(s), fn, hint or "", true) then return end if U.has("echoLink") then echoLink(win, plain(s), fn, hint or "", true) return end U.outw(win, s) end
function U.killhandler(id) if id and U.has("killAnonymousEventHandler") then pcall(killAnonymousEventHandler, id) end end
-- Repeating timer built on tempTimer, which is C++ and definitely there. -- registerNamedTimer would do this too, but it's Lua-side and unverifiable, and -- a self-rearming tempTimer keyed on a generation counter is no more code. U.timers = U.timers or {}
-- The generation counter is what lets U.unevery cancel a chain, but it also -- means a second caller using the same key silently stops the first: its tick -- sees a bumped generation and just doesn't rearm. Re-arming your OWN timer is -- the normal case, so only say something when the function is a different one. U.timerfn = U.timerfn or {}
function U.every(key, secs, fn) if U.timerfn[key] and U.timerfn[key] ~= fn and U.timers[key] then U.warn("timer '" .. tostring(key) .. "' is already in use - the earlier one has stopped") end U.timerfn[key] = fn U.timers[key] = (U.timers[key] or 0) + 1 local gen = U.timers[key] local function tick() if U.timers[key] ~= gen then return end -- superseded or cancelled local ok, err = pcall(fn) if not ok then U.err("timer " .. key .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end if U.timers[key] == gen then tempTimer(secs, tick) end end tempTimer(secs, tick) end
function U.unevery(key) U.timers[key] = (U.timers[key] or 0) + 1 -- orphans any tick in flight end
-- The prefix on everything the client says. It used to be "[aardkit]" on every -- line, which is the same nine characters repeated forever and tells you nothing -- you didn't know - you typed the command. The module's own name is information: -- when a warning arrives unprompted mid-fight, which part is talking is the -- first thing you want. -- -- Padded to a common width so the messages line up rather than stepping in and -- out with the length of the name. local TAGW = 11
local function tagof(label) local t = "[" .. label .. "]" local pad = TAGW - #t return "<#7aa2f7>[<#e94560>" .. label .. "<#7aa2f7>]<r>" .. string.rep(" ", pad > 0 and pad or 1) end
local TAG = tagof("aardkit")
function U.note(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#c8d0dc>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.ok(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#9ece6a>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.warn(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#e0af68>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
function U.err(msg) U.out("\n" .. TAG .. "<#f7768e>" .. msg .. "<r>") end
-- A module-scoped view of U. Same functions, except the four that print carry -- the module's own name; everything else falls through by metatable, so a module -- changes one line at the top and not a single call site. local named = {}
function U.named(label) label = tostring(label or "aardkit") if named[label] then return named[label] end local tag = tagof(label) local t = setmetatable({}, { __index = U }) t.note = function(m) U.out("\n" .. tag .. "<#c8d0dc>" .. tostring(m) .. "<r>") end t.ok = function(m) U.out("\n" .. tag .. "<#9ece6a>" .. tostring(m) .. "<r>") end t.warn = function(m) U.out("\n" .. tag .. "<#e0af68>" .. tostring(m) .. "<r>") end t.err = function(m) U.out("\n" .. tag .. "<#f7768e>" .. tostring(m) .. "<r>") end named[label] = t return t end
-- help blocks: pass a list of {cmd, description} and it lines them up -- The left column is padded to the widest label, which is right until one entry -- is enormous - 'loot api | auth | upload | update | resync yes' is 45 -- characters and pushed every description in the block far enough right to wrap -- off the edge of the screen, which is what made the loot help look truncated. -- So the padding is capped, and anything past the cap gets its description on -- the next line rather than dragging the other thirty rows with it. local HELP_CAP = 32
function U.help(title, rows) U.out("\n<#7aa2f7>" .. title .. "<r>") local w = 0 for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if r[2] and #r[1] <= HELP_CAP then w = math.max(w, #r[1]) end end for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if not r[2] then U.out("\n <#8a93a8>" .. r[1] .. "<r>") elseif #r[1] > w then U.out("\n <#e0af68>" .. r[1] .. "<r>") U.out("\n " .. string.rep(" ", w) .. " <#c8d0dc>" .. r[2] .. "<r>") else U.out("\n <#e0af68>" .. r[1] .. string.rep(" ", w - #r[1]) .. "<r> <#c8d0dc>" .. r[2] .. "<r>") end end echo("\n") end
--- -- strings ---
-- A bordered table, the shape the MUSHclient mapper prints its lists in: -- -- +------------+--------------------+---------+ -- | area | room name | rm uid | -- +------------+--------------------+---------+ -- | bootcamp | The Common Room | 47195 | -- +------------+--------------------+---------+ -- -- Worth having in core rather than in whichever module wanted it first. A -- two-column U.help is right for a list of commands and wrong for anything with -- three facts per row, and "you can read it at a glance" is most of why that -- mapper's output is missed. -- -- It FITS THE WINDOW. A grid that wraps is worse than no grid - the borders -- land mid-row and the columns stop lining up, which is the one thing a table -- is for. So the width is measured, and a column marked `flex` gives up -- whatever the fixed ones need. If it still won't fit, the flex column shrinks -- to a floor and the row is cut there. -- -- cols: { { title, align = "l"|"r", max = <chars>, flex = true }, ... } -- rows: lists of values; a row may carry .link = { label, command, hint } function U.table(cols, rows, foot) -- The wrap setting, not the console width. Text wraps at getWindowWrap -- whatever size the window is - a 200-column console wrapping at 100 still -- breaks the grid at 100 - so that's the number that matters, and -- getColumnCount is only the fallback for a Mudlet without it. -- -- Read every time it renders rather than cached, which is the whole of -- being responsive here: resize the window, run the command again, it fits. local avail for _, fn in ipairs({ "getWindowWrap", "getColumnCount" }) do if not avail and U.has(fn) then local ok, n = pcall(_G[fn], "main") n = ok and tonumber(n) or nil if n and n > 20 then avail = n end end end avail = (avail or 100) - 2 -- two back, so a full row never touches the edge
-- a trailing [del] sits outside the grid but still takes room on the line local linked = false for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if type(r.link) == "table" then linked = true; break end end if linked then avail = avail - 7 end
-- Cut with a marker, so a value that CONTINUES doesn't read as one that -- ended. 'get bus bag' and 'get bus bag;unlock down;...' are different -- exits and the difference has to survive the column. -- -- '...' and not the single '…' character: every width here is counted with -- #, which counts BYTES, so a three-byte ellipsis would look like one column -- and occupy three. Three full stops are three of each and the arithmetic -- holds. The marker replaces the last three characters of the value rather -- than being added to it, so the cell is exactly as wide as it says. local function cut(v, n) if n < 1 then return "" end if #v <= n then return v end if n <= 3 then return string.rep(".", n) end return v:sub(1, n - 3) .. "..." end
local function cell(c, v) v = tostring(v == nil and "" or v) if c.max then v = cut(v, c.max) end return v end
local w, flex = {}, nil for i, c in ipairs(cols) do w[i] = #tostring(c[1] or "") if c.flex then flex = i end end for _, r in ipairs(rows) do for i, c in ipairs(cols) do local n = #cell(c, r[i]) if n > w[i] then w[i] = n end end end
-- '| ' + ' ' per column, plus the closing '|' local function total() local t = 1 for i = 1, #cols do t = t + w[i] + 3 end return t end
if flex and total() > avail then w[flex] = math.max(8, w[flex] - (total() - avail)) end -- still over: take it out of the widest non-flex text column while total() > avail do local widest, at = 0, nil for i, c in ipairs(cols) do if i ~= flex and c.align ~= "r" and w[i] > widest then widest, at = w[i], i end end if not at or widest <= 6 then break end w[at] = w[at] - 1 end
local function rule() local p = {} for i = 1, #cols do p[i] = string.rep("-", w[i] + 2) end return "+" .. table.concat(p, "+") .. "+" end
local function line(vals, colour) local p = {} for i, c in ipairs(cols) do local v = cut(cell(c, vals[i]), w[i]) local pad = string.rep(" ", w[i] - #v) p[i] = " " .. (c.align == "r" and (pad .. v) or (v .. pad)) .. " " end return "<#3a4a6b>|<r><" .. colour .. ">" .. table.concat(p, "<r><#3a4a6b>|<r><" .. colour .. ">") .. "<r><#3a4a6b>|<r>" end
local head = {} for i, c in ipairs(cols) do head[i] = c[1] end
U.out("\n<#3a4a6b>" .. rule() .. "<r>") U.out("\n" .. line(head, "#7aa2f7")) U.out("\n<#3a4a6b>" .. rule() .. "<r>") for _, r in ipairs(rows) do U.out("\n" .. line(r, "#c8d0dc")) -- Appended after the closing bar rather than put in a cell: a link has -- no printable width the column arithmetic can account for, and one -- inside a cell breaks the grid the table exists to keep. if type(r.link) == "table" and r.link[1] then U.outLink(" " .. r.link[1], r.link[2], r.link[3], true) end end U.out("\n<#3a4a6b>" .. rule() .. "<r>") if foot then U.out("\n<#8a93a8>" .. foot .. "<r>") end echo("\n") end
function U.trim(s) return (tostring(s or ""):gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "")) end
-- "buffer 200" -> "buffer", "200" function U.split_verb(s) s = U.trim(s) local verb, rest = s:match("^(%S+)%s*(.*)$") return (verb or ""):lower(), rest or "" end
-- db: stores numeric columns as REAL, so a room id reads back 16298.0 function U.rid(n) return string.format("%d", math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) end
function U.commas(n) local s = tostring(math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) local out = s:reverse():gsub("(%d%d%d)", "%1,"):reverse() return (out:gsub("^,", "")) end
-- 4211 -> "1h 10m", for last-seen columns function U.duration(secs) secs = math.floor(tonumber(secs) or 0) if secs < 60 then return secs .. "s" end local m = math.floor(secs / 60) if m < 60 then return m .. "m" end local h = math.floor(m / 60) if h < 24 then return h .. "h " .. (m % 60) .. "m" end return math.floor(h / 24) .. "d " .. (h % 24) .. "h" end
-- Aardwolf sends colour codes as @x123 / @R etc in some channels; strip for storage function U.strip_codes(s) s = tostring(s or "") s = s:gsub("@x%d%d?%d?", ""):gsub("@[%a@]", "") return s end
-- Aardwolf @ codes -> hex, for rendering a stored/echoed @-coded string locally local ACOLOR = { r = "#800000", R = "#ff0000", g = "#008000", G = "#00ff00", y = "#808000", Y = "#ffff00", b = "#000080", B = "#0000ff", m = "#800080", M = "#ff00ff", c = "#008080", C = "#00ffff", w = "#c0c0c0", W = "#ffffff", D = "#808080", }
-- xterm 256 -> hex, the standard cube + greyscale ramp local function xterm(n) n = tonumber(n) or 0 if n < 16 then local basic = { "#000000", "#800000", "#008000", "#808000", "#000080", "#800080", "#008080", "#c0c0c0", "#808080", "#ff0000", "#00ff00", "#ffff00", "#0000ff", "#ff00ff", "#00ffff", "#ffffff" } return basic[n + 1] or "#c0c0c0" end if n < 232 then local i = n - 16 local lv = { 0, 95, 135, 175, 215, 255 } return string.format("#%02x%02x%02x", lv[math.floor(i / 36) % 6 + 1], lv[math.floor(i / 6) % 6 + 1], lv[i % 6 + 1]) end local g = 8 + (n - 232) * 10 return string.format("#%02x%02x%02x", g, g, g) end
-- turn an @-coded string into something cecho understands. $C is a server-side -- channel reset the codes don't cover, so locally it just reads as white. function U.acolor(s) s = tostring(s or ""):gsub("%$C", "@w") s = s:gsub("@x(%d%d?%d?)", function(n) return "<" .. xterm(n) .. ">" end) s = s:gsub("@(%a)", function(c) return ACOLOR[c] and ("<" .. ACOLOR[c] .. ">") or "" end) return (s:gsub("@@", "@")) end
function U.aecho(s) U.out("\n" .. U.acolor(s) .. "<r>") end
--- -- gmcp ---
-- current room vnum, or nil if gmcp hasn't landed yet function U.room() local r = gmcp and gmcp.room and gmcp.room.info if not r then return nil end return tonumber(r.num), r.name, r.zone end
function U.charname() local c = gmcp and gmcp.char and gmcp.char.base and gmcp.char.base.name return c or getProfileName() end
-- Aardwolf sets char.status.state: 3 is in the game, 8 is in the game and -- fighting. This accepted only 3, so "am I playing" answered no for the whole -- of every fight. Healme's watcher bailed on its first line on every combat -- tick and never drank while anything was hitting you - which is the one time -- it's for. Confirmed off a live 'healme raw' mid-fight (state 8, pos -- "Fighting", enemy named) and off the stock module, which branches on -- state == 8 for in-combat in four separate keybinds. -- -- Anything wanting "in the game and NOT fighting" wants U.fighting() below, -- not this. Spellups already had its own check and is unaffected. function U.playing() local st = tonumber(gmcp and gmcp.char and gmcp.char.status and gmcp.char.status.state) return st == 3 or st == 8 end
-- Run fn once the character is actually in the game, not merely connected. -- -- sysConnectionEvent is the socket opening. The name and password prompts come -- after it, so anything sent in that window is typed into one of them - and a -- password prompt echoes nothing back, so a module command sent there is taken -- as the password, the login fails, and there is nothing on screen saying why. -- -- char.status arriving isn't enough either: Aardwolf sends it during the login -- sequence, with state 1 and 2. Only 3, or 8 for fighting, means you're in. -- -- Prefer not sending at all - a refresh button the player presses beats a -- command the client decides to send. This is for the cases that genuinely have -- to talk to the MUD by themselves. local ready_q = {}
function U.ready(fn) if type(fn) ~= "function" then return end if U.playing() then fn(); return end ready_q[#ready_q + 1] = fn end
local function drain_ready() if not U.playing() then return end if #ready_q == 0 then return end local q = ready_q ready_q = {} for _, fn in ipairs(q) do local ok, err = pcall(fn) if not ok then U.err("deferred until login: " .. tostring(err)) end end end
U.killhandler(aardkit_util_ready_handler) aardkit_util_ready_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("gmcp.char.status", drain_ready)
--- -- nothing goes to the MUD before you're in it -- -- This has bitten twice now. sysConnectionEvent is the socket opening; the name -- and password prompts come after it, and a password prompt echoes nothing back -- - so a scripted command landing in that window IS the password, the login -- fails, and there is nothing on screen saying why. Last time it was helpwin's -- telnet negotiation on a 2s timer. This time I could not find the sender at -- all, having read every send() and every connection handler in the suite. -- -- So stop looking for the culprit and make the window unreachable. Anything -- sent before char.status says 3 or 8 is held and goes out the moment you're -- in, and it says what it held so the next one names itself. -- -- Safe for autologin: Mudlet sends the name and password from C++, through -- cTelnet, not through this Lua function. Typing in the command line doesn't -- come through here either. Only SCRIPTED sends do, and a scripted send before -- login is a bug every time. -- -- Wrapped once. A rebuild re-runs this file, and wrapping the wrapper would -- queue behind a queue. if not aardkit_send_guarded then aardkit_send_guarded = true local real_send = send
send = function(what, echoBack) if U.playing() then return real_send(what, echoBack) end U.warn("held '" .. tostring(what) .. "' - not in the game yet." .. " It'll go when you are. (A scripted send before login is what" .. " gets typed into the password prompt.)") U.ready(function() real_send(what, echoBack) end) return true end end
-- In combat, in the MUD's own words. Three signals because no one of them -- holds on its own: state is 8 while fighting, enemy carries the name for as -- long as it lasts, and enemypct is the fallback. -- -- enemy arrives as "" and as "none" when there's nobody, and enemypct arrives -- as an empty string - so `tonumber(x or 0) > 0` never sees its `or 0` (in Lua -- "" is truthy), gets nil out of tonumber, and raises comparing nil to a -- number. That's how healme's combat mode failed: silently, inside the gmcp -- watcher's pcall, on every tick. One copy here so that only had to be worked -- out once. function U.fighting() local st = gmcp and gmcp.char and gmcp.char.status if not st then return false end if tonumber(st.state) == 8 then return true end local e = st.enemy if e ~= nil and e ~= "" and e ~= "none" then return true end return (tonumber(tostring(st.enemypct or "")) or 0) > 0 end

Script.name: 10_panel
Script.script:
--[[ aardkit panel manager Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
Every ported plugin that used to draw a MUSHclient miniwindow gets one of these instead. Two modes:
embed - Adjustable.Container inside the main window. Drag the title bar, drag the edges to resize, right-click for the built-in menu. The container saves and reloads its own geometry. dock - Geyser.UserWindow, a real Qt dock widget. Drag it out to float, drag it back to dock it to any edge. Mudlet stores that layout in windowLayout.dat by itself.
Which mode each panel is in (and whether it's hidden) is ours to remember, so a panel comes back the way you left it. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.panel = aardkit.panel or {}
local P = aardkit.panel local U = aardkit.util.named("Panels")
P.reg = P.reg or {} -- name -> panel P.state = P.state or {} -- name -> {mode=, hidden=}
local DEFAULT_MODE = "embed"
-- Doubles as the title bar height: Adjustable.Container places contents at -- padding*2. Mudlet's own default is 10; the close/minimise buttons are 15px -- tall sitting at y=4, so anything under 10 clips them and the title too. local TITLEBAR = 10
local STYLE = { bg = "#0d1117", bar = "#161b2e", border = "#3a4a6b", title = "#e94560", text = "#c8d0dc", }
-- 235 rather than 255 so a panel sits on the output rather than blotting it. -- -- `clear` drops it to nothing, and exists for exactly one case: Mudlet's map. -- An embedded map is NOT a child of the container it appears to live in - -- createMapper draws it at absolute coordinates in the main window - so the -- container's background is painted OVER the map rather than behind it. At -- alpha 235 that reads as the map having gone dim, and any repaint of the map -- brings it forward and it looks fine again. It isn't a fade: it's a tinted -- sheet of glass that the map keeps coming back through. -- Opaque. It was 235 - a deliberate 92%, so a panel "sat on the output rather -- than blotting it" - and in practice that means the game text shows through -- every panel you own, which reads as a rendering fault rather than a choice. -- 'panel opacity <0-255>' brings it back for anyone who wants it. -- The default every panel inherits. A panel may override it, and the override -- wins; unset an override and it goes back to following this. P.opacity = 255
-- Drag a floating dockable window to an edge of the main window and Mudlet -- attaches it there. On by default, because dragging a panel into place beats -- typing where it goes. -- -- Geyser says setDockPosition "works also if autoDock is disabled", so turning -- this off costs the drag gesture and nothing else - 'gauges dock bottom' still -- docks either way. One panel can override the default, the way opacity does. -- -- It has nothing to do with the blue four-way arrows over the game window, which -- I first blamed it for. Those are the STOCK module's: GUIframe puts a 30x30 -- resize grip on each enabled side, blue_arrows_30t.png at rest and -- blue_arrows.png on hover, and they go when that module does. P.autodock = true
-- Scrollbars off. Every panel console was built with one since the initial -- import; they only ever looked absent because the stock module's app-wide -- stylesheet drew them on black, and that left with the module. A panel you -- scroll with the wheel does not need a visible bar taking a column. P.scrollbars = false
-- Alpha as a PERCENTAGE, which is what Qt takes and what Mudlet's own Geyser -- writes (GeyserAdjustableContainer.lua: "rgba(0,0,0,100%)"). -- -- We were emitting rgba(13,17,23,255). Qt follows CSS3, where the alpha is 0-1 -- or a percentage, so 255 is out of range and the whole background-color -- declaration is DISCARDED - leaving the panel with no background at all. That -- is the see-through, and it looked like a subtle opacity bug rather than a -- syntax error because the border and radius on the following lines still -- applied. It also explains why `clear` worked: alpha 0 is in range. -- -- A fully opaque panel gets plain hex with no alpha channel at all, so there is -- nothing left to misparse in the common case. local function container_style(clear, alpha) alpha = clear and 0 or math.max(0, math.min(255, tonumber(alpha or P.opacity) or 255)) local fill = (alpha >= 255) and STYLE.bg or string.format("rgba(13,17,23,%d%%)", math.floor(alpha / 255 * 100 + 0.5)) return [[ background-color: ]] .. fill .. [[; border: 1px solid ]] .. STYLE.border .. [[; border-radius: 3px; ]] end
--- -- state ---
local function load_state() P.state = U.load("panels", {}) local sb = P.state["_scrollbars"] if sb and sb.value ~= nil then P.scrollbars = sb.value and true or false end local saved = P.state["_opacity"] if type(saved) == "table" and tonumber(saved.value) then P.opacity = math.floor(tonumber(saved.value)) end end
local function save_state() U.save("panels", P.state) end
local function st(name) P.state[name] = P.state[name] or {} return P.state[name] end
--- -- buffer migration — carry the scrollback (with its colours) across a mode flip ---
local function migrate(from, to) if not from or not to then return end local n = getLineCount(from) if not n or n < 1 then return end local first = math.max(1, n - 500) -- 500 lines is plenty to carry over for i = first, n - 1 do moveCursor(from, 0, i) selectCurrentLine(from) copy(from) appendBuffer(to) end moveCursorEnd(from) end
--- -- panel ---
local Panel = {} Panel.__index = Panel
-- Mudlet's borders carve the CONSOLE out of the main window, and Geyser -- measures against the main window - the two are not the same rectangle. -- getBorderLeft/Right/Top/Bottom exist in Mudlet 4.22 but appear nowhere in -- mudlet-lua, so guard them: an older build gets the old full-width behaviour -- rather than a strip clipped to nothing. local function border(side) local fn = _G["getBorder" .. side] if type(fn) ~= "function" then return 0 end local ok, n = pcall(fn) return (ok and tonumber(n)) or 0 end
local function setborder(side, n) pcall(_G["setBorder" .. side], n) end
-- The MAIN console's scrollbar is not ours to remove, so it still gets a theme -- that matches the panels rather than Qt's own chrome. The stock module's -- styleLoad() did this app-wide and was the only setAppStyleSheet in the -- profile, which is why every bar looked invisible until it left. -- -- The tag namespaces it on Mudlet builds that take one, and is harmlessly -- ignored on those that don't. local function scrollbar_style() local css = ([[ QScrollBar:vertical { background: %s; width: 10px; margin: 0px; border: 0px; } QScrollBar::handle:vertical { background: %s; min-height: 20px; border-radius: 4px; } QScrollBar::handle:vertical:hover { background: %s; } QScrollBar::add-line:vertical, QScrollBar::sub-line:vertical { height: 0px; border: 0px; } QScrollBar::add-page:vertical, QScrollBar::sub-page:vertical { background: %s; } QScrollBar:horizontal { background: %s; height: 10px; margin: 0px; border: 0px; } QScrollBar::handle:horizontal { background: %s; min-width: 20px; border-radius: 4px; } QScrollBar::add-line:horizontal, QScrollBar::sub-line:horizontal { width: 0px; border: 0px; } QScrollBar::add-page:horizontal, QScrollBar::sub-page:horizontal { background: %s; } ]]):format(STYLE.bg, STYLE.border, STYLE.title, STYLE.bg, STYLE.bg, STYLE.border, STYLE.bg) pcall(setAppStyleSheet, css, "aardkit") end
P.scrollbar_style = scrollbar_style
local function rgb(hex) hex = tostring(hex or ""):gsub("#", "") return tonumber(hex:sub(1, 2), 16) or 0, tonumber(hex:sub(3, 4), 16) or 0, tonumber(hex:sub(5, 6), 16) or 0 end
-- Geyser defines setColor on Button and Gauge and nowhere else; a MiniConsole -- reaches one through inheritance and takes a hex STRING, which is the shape of -- call that quietly does nothing. setBackgroundColor takes numbers and an -- explicit alpha, so the panel is opaque because it was told to be rather than -- because nothing made it transparent. local function opaque(console) if type(console) ~= "table" or type(console.name) ~= "string" then return end local r, g, b = rgb(STYLE.bg) pcall(setBackgroundColor, console.name, r, g, b, 255) end
P.opaque = opaque
-- public so the harness can read the CSS rather than the fact of a call P.container_style = container_style
-- One place, so chat's eight tab consoles follow the same setting as everything -- else rather than keeping the bar they were built with. function P.scrollbar(console) if type(console) ~= "table" or type(console.name) ~= "string" then return end pcall(P.scrollbars and enableScrollBar or disableScrollBar, console.name) end
function Panel:_build() local s = st(self.name) local mode = s.mode or self.defmode
-- bumped every rebuild so widget names stay unique; Mudlet keeps the old -- label objects alive and reusing a name orphans them self.gen = (self.gen or 0) + 1
-- "frame": in the main window's own border, which is where the stock module -- puts its bars and the only placement that sits ABOVE the command line. -- -- Mudlet's UserWindow docking is a different thing: "dock bottom" attaches a -- separate window under everything, command line included. setBorder* -- shrinks the console instead and leaves a strip that belongs to us, which -- is what their guiLoad does - setBorderBottom(bottomStartHeight + offset). -- -- Geyser reads a negative coordinate as an offset from the far edge, so -- y = -h lands the container in the strip we just reserved. if mode == "frame" then local side = st(self.name).framepos or "bottom" local h = tonumber(st(self.name).framesize) or self.h or 56 local cons = { name = self.name .. "_fr" .. self.gen }
-- Claim our own side FIRST, so the reads below see this panel's strip -- rather than whatever was there before. setborder(side:sub(1, 1):upper() .. side:sub(2), h)
-- Then measure against the console box. A bottom strip at x=0 -- width="100%" spans the whole WINDOW - it ran underneath the 405px -- right column the stock module left reserved. Geyser takes -- "100%-460" as scale 1.0 with a -460 offset, so the strip ends flush -- with the console's right edge and follows a window resize. local l, r = border("Left"), border("Right") local t, b = border("Top"), border("Bottom") if side == "bottom" then cons.x, cons.y = l, -h cons.width, cons.height = "100%-" .. (l + r), h elseif side == "top" then cons.x, cons.y = l, 0 cons.width, cons.height = "100%-" .. (l + r), h elseif side == "left" then cons.x, cons.y = 0, t cons.width, cons.height = h, "100%-" .. (t + b) else cons.x, cons.y = -h, t cons.width, cons.height = h, "100%-" .. (t + b) end self.holder = Geyser.Container:new(cons)
elseif mode == "dock" then -- Mudlet docks a UserWindow to an edge of the main window, which is -- where the stock module nails its own bars. autoDock is on by default -- and is what puts the crosshairs up when you drag one over the game -- window - so a floating panel can be dropped onto an edge by hand and -- Mudlet remembers it. -- -- docked=true is only passed when an edge was actually asked for: -- Geyser forces dockPosition to "floating" when docked is false, and -- that is the behaviour every panel had before this. local pos = st(self.name).dockpos local cons = { name = self.name .. "_uw" .. self.gen, titleText = self.title, autoDock = self:autodock(), } if pos and pos ~= "floating" then cons.docked, cons.dockPosition = true, pos end self.holder = Geyser.UserWindow:new(cons) else self.holder = Adjustable.Container:new({ name = self.name .. "_ac" .. self.gen, x = self.x, y = self.y, width = self.w, height = self.h, titleText = self.title, titleTxtColor = STYLE.title, adjLabelstyle = container_style(self.clear, self:alpha()), padding = TITLEBAR, autoSave = true, autoLoad = true, })
-- Adjustable.Container puts its contents at y = padding*2 and draws the -- title above that, so padding IS the title bar height. At 4 that left -- 8px for a 12px title and the console covered it. Worse, padding is -- saved with the geometry and restored on load, so the constructor value -- above gets overwritten by whatever the file remembers - it has to be -- set again afterwards or old saves keep the cramped bar forever. if self.holder.setPadding then pcall(function() self.holder:setPadding(TITLEBAR) end) end end
self.mode = mode
-- Measure and parent against the CONTENT box, not the outer frame. An -- Adjustable.Container's Inside starts at x=padding, so anything that sized -- itself off the outer width then drew from that offset origin overhung the -- right edge by exactly padding - which is why the recall buttons ran past -- the border, and why raising padding to 10 made it worse. self.container = type(self.holder.Inside) == "table" and self.holder.Inside or self.holder
if not self.consoleless then local old = self.console and self.console.name self.console = Geyser.MiniConsole:new({ name = self.name .. "_con" .. self.gen, x = 0, y = 0, width = "100%", height = "100%", autoWrap = self.wrap ~= false, color = STYLE.bg, fontSize = self.fontSize or 9, scrollBar = true, }, self.holder) self.console:setColor(STYLE.bg) opaque(self.console) P.scrollbar(self.console) if old then migrate(old, self.console.name) end end
if self.onbuild then local ok, err = pcall(self.onbuild, self) if not ok then U.err("panel " .. self.name .. " onbuild: " .. tostring(err)) end end end
-- This panel's own setting if it has one, otherwise the shared default. function Panel:alpha() local own = st(self.name).opacity return tonumber(own) or P.opacity end
function Panel:restyle() if self.holder and self.holder.setStyleSheet then pcall(function() self.holder:setStyleSheet(container_style(self.clear, self:alpha())) end) end end
function Panel:show() self.holder:show() self:raise() st(self.name).hidden = false save_state() end
function Panel:hide() self.holder:hide() st(self.name).hidden = true save_state() end
function Panel:visible() return not st(self.name).hidden end
function Panel:toggle() if self:visible() then self:hide() else self:show() end end
local DOCKPOS = { top = true, bottom = true, left = true, right = true, floating = true }
-- The shared setting unless this panel has said otherwise. function Panel:autodock() local own = st(self.name).autodock if own ~= nil then return own end return P.autodock end
-- Where a docked panel sits. Changing it live works when the window already -- exists; otherwise it takes on the next build, which setmode does anyway. -- Live where Mudlet allows it: enableAutoDock/disableAutoDock exist on a -- UserWindow, so an already-open window doesn't need rebuilding to lose its -- arrows. Returns 1 if it took, so the caller can say how many moved. -- Put one panel back the way it started. Its own state goes, and so does the -- geometry Adjustable.Container saved for it - a panel dragged off-screen or -- docked somewhere unhelpful is otherwise stuck there across reloads, because -- both halves have to agree before it comes back. function Panel:reset() -- same debt as setmode: a reset out of frame mode must release the border if self.mode == "frame" then local had = st(self.name).framepos if had then setborder(had:sub(1, 1):upper() .. had:sub(2), 0) end end P.state[self.name] = nil save_state() for gen = 1, (self.gen or 1) + 1 do os.remove(getMudletHomeDir() .. "/AdjustableContainer/" .. self.name .. "_ac" .. gen .. ".lua") end self:_build() self:show() U.ok(self.name .. " reset - back where it started.") end
function Panel:apply_autodock() local w = self.holder if self.mode ~= "dock" or type(w) ~= "table" then return 0 end local on = self:autodock() local fn = on and w.enableAutoDock or w.disableAutoDock if type(fn) == "function" and pcall(function() fn(w) end) then return 1 end return 0 end
function Panel:setdock(pos) pos = tostring(pos or ""):lower() if not DOCKPOS[pos] then U.warn("dock position must be one of: " .. table.concat({ "top", "bottom", "left", "right", "floating" }, " ")) return end st(self.name).dockpos = pos save_state() if self.mode ~= "dock" then self:setmode("dock") return end local w = self.holder if type(w) == "table" and type(w.setDockPosition) == "function" and pcall(function() w:setDockPosition(pos) end) then U.ok(self.name .. " docked " .. pos .. ".") else self:_build() U.ok(self.name .. " docked " .. pos .. ".") end end
local FRAMEPOS = { top = true, bottom = true, left = true, right = true }
-- Into the main window's border, above the command line. Give back whatever -- border we took when it leaves, or the console stays short for the session. function Panel:setframe(side, size) side = tostring(side or "bottom"):lower() if side == "off" or side == "none" then local had = st(self.name).framepos st(self.name).framepos, st(self.name).framesize = nil, nil if had then pcall(_G["setBorder" .. had:sub(1,1):upper() .. had:sub(2)], 0) end self:setmode("embed") return end if not FRAMEPOS[side] then U.warn("frame side must be top, bottom, left, right - or off") return end st(self.name).framepos = side st(self.name).framesize = tonumber(size) or st(self.name).framesize or self.h or 56 save_state() if self.mode == "frame" then self:_build() else self:setmode("frame") end U.ok(self.name .. " in the " .. side .. " border, above the command line.") end
function Panel:setmode(mode) if mode ~= "dock" and mode ~= "embed" and mode ~= "frame" then U.warn("panel mode must be dock, embed or frame") return end if mode == self.mode then return end
-- Leaving frame mode by any route has to hand the border back. Only -- setframe("off") did, so 'panel gauges embed' left the strip reserved for -- good - and Mudlet writes border sizes to the profile, so "for good" meant -- across restarts. That is how the stock module's 405px right column -- outlived the stock module. if self.mode == "frame" and mode ~= "frame" then local had = st(self.name).framepos if had then setborder(had:sub(1, 1):upper() .. had:sub(2), 0) end end
local oldholder, oldcon = self.holder, self.console st(self.name).mode = mode self:_build()
-- The new console pulled the scrollback across in _build, so the old shell -- is finished. Hiding it only made it invisible - the Geyser objects, their -- Mudlet windows and their click callbacks all stayed alive, so every -- dock/embed toggle left another full widget tree behind for the session. -- Geyser.Container:delete() is real (geyser/GeyserContainer.lua:388); pcall -- it anyway because not every class inherits it. local function drop(o) if type(o) ~= "table" then return end if type(o.delete) == "function" and pcall(function() o:delete() end) then return end pcall(function() o:hide() end) end drop(oldcon) drop(oldholder)
if self:visible() then self:show() else self:hide() end save_state() U.ok(self.name .. " -> " .. mode) end
-- The AardwolfMudlet GUI frame builds after us and lands on top, which is how a -- panel gets "lost" under the chat tabs. -- -- raiseWindow() needs a REAL widget name. A Geyser container isn't one - only -- the labels and consoles inside it are actual Mudlet windows - so raising the -- container by name silently does nothing. -- -- Order matters and it bit us: raiseWindow puts a widget on TOP, so whoever is -- raised last wins. Walking windowList with pairs() is a random order, so some -- runs raised the container's own backdrop last and painted it over the panel's -- own contents. The buttons were never missing - they were under a 92%-opaque -- label, which is exactly what "faded and unclickable" looks like. So: backdrop -- first, contents next, chrome last, every time. function Panel:raise() local h = self.holder if not h then return end
local function up(o) if type(o) == "table" and type(o.name) == "string" then pcall(raiseWindow, o.name) end end
up(h.adjLabel) -- backdrop + title, bottom of our stack
local seen = {} local function contents(o, depth) if type(o) ~= "table" or depth > 4 or seen[o] then return end seen[o] = true up(o) -- Geyser keeps children twice: windowList keyed by name, and windows as -- an ORDERED array. pairs() over the first is hash order, so every -- raise re-rolled the z-order inside the panel - which is how Chat's -- opaque backdrop kept landing on top of its own tabs, hiding a -- different arbitrary subset each time. Geyser's own raiseAll walks the -- ordered array for exactly this reason. if type(o.windowList) == "table" then if type(o.windows) == "table" and #o.windows > 0 then for i = 1, #o.windows do contents(o.windowList[o.windows[i]], depth + 1) end else for _, child in pairs(o.windowList) do contents(child, depth + 1) end end end end contents(h.Inside, 0) contents(self.console, 0)
-- minimise/close have to stay clickable above everything we just raised up(h.minimizeLabel) up(h.exitLabel)
-- A transient panel is on screen because something just put it there and -- you are reading it right now. Anything else coming forward - a repaint, -- the layout sweep on load, dragging another panel - would otherwise land -- on top of what you asked to see. So whenever a normal panel raises, the -- transient ones go back above it. if not self.transient then for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p ~= self and p.transient and p:visible() then p:raise() end end end end
function Panel:cecho(s) if self.console then aardkit.util.outw(self.console.name, s) end end
function Panel:echo(s) if self.console then self.console:echo(s) end end
function Panel:clear() if self.console then self.console:clear() end end
--- -- paging -- -- A Mudlet console that is scrolled up splits into a scrollback pane and a live -- pane with a divider across it. That split IS what being scrolled up looks -- like and nothing turns it off - no setConfig key, no console method, no -- upperPane symbol in the binary. Right for the MUD window, where you want to -- keep reading while new text arrives. Wrong for a document, which has an end -- and doesn't move. -- -- So a paged panel keeps the whole thing in an off-screen createBuffer and -- shows one screenful copied out of it. Never scrolled, so never split, and -- page one is the top. The buffer is also what keeps the colours: copy() and -- appendBuffer move a line with its formatting intact. ---
local PAGE_H = 20
function Panel:page_begin() self.store = self.store or ("aardkit_" .. self.name .. "_buffer") pcall(createBuffer, self.store) -- a no-op once it exists pcall(clearWindow, self.store) self.total, self.page, self.pages = 0, 1, 1 if self.console then pcall(clearWindow, self.console.name) end end
-- copy the line the current trigger fired on into the store, colours and all function Panel:page_add() if not self.store then return end selectCurrentLine() copy() appendBuffer(self.store) end
function Panel:page_end() if not self.store then return end local ok, n = pcall(getLineCount, self.store) self.total = (ok and type(n) == "number") and n or 0 self.page = 1 self:page_paint() end
-- how many lines fit. getRowCount is the console's own answer and the only one -- that stays right as the panel is dragged about; the fallback is for the -- moment before it has been laid out. local function rows_of(p) if not p.console then return 20 end local ok, n = pcall(getRowCount, p.console.name) if ok and type(n) == "number" and n > 0 then return n end return 20 end
function Panel:page_paint() local c = self.console if not (c and self.container and self.store) then return end
local per = math.max(1, rows_of(self)) self.total = self.total or 0 self.pages = math.max(1, math.ceil(self.total / per)) self.page = math.min(math.max(1, self.page or 1), self.pages)
local h = U.px(self.container.get_height and self.container:get_height() or self.container.height) local w = U.px(self.container.get_width and self.container:get_width() or self.container.width) if w < 60 then w = 600 end
pcall(function() c:move(0, 0) c:resize("100%", "-" .. PAGE_H .. "px") end)
pcall(clearWindow, c.name) local first = (self.page - 1) * per local last = math.min(self.total - 1, first + per - 1) for i = first, last do moveCursor(self.store, 0, i) selectCurrentLine(self.store) copy(self.store) appendBuffer(c.name) end
self.pagebtn = self.pagebtn or {} local function btn(key, cb, arg) if not self.pagebtn[key] then self.pagebtn[key] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_" .. self.name .. "_pg_" .. key .. "_" .. (self.gen or 1), x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = PAGE_H - 2, }, self.container) if cb then self.pagebtn[key]:setClickCallback(cb, arg) end end return self.pagebtn[key] end local function style(on) return string.format("background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-radius: 3px;", on and "#1b2540" or "#141b2d", on and "#3a4a6b" or "#232c44") end local function lab(on, s) return string.format("<center><span style='color:%s'>%s</span></center>", on and "#c8d0dc" or "#4a5468", s) end
local y, bw = math.max(0, h - PAGE_H), 70 local back = self.page > 1 local fwd = self.page < self.pages
local b = btn("prev", "aardkit.panel.page_prev", self.name) b:move(4, y); b:resize(bw, PAGE_H - 2) b:setStyleSheet(style(back)); b:echo(lab(back, "< prev")); b:show()
b = btn("next", "aardkit.panel.page_next", self.name) b:move(w - bw - 4, y); b:resize(bw, PAGE_H - 2) b:setStyleSheet(style(fwd)); b:echo(lab(fwd, "next >")); b:show()
b = btn("count") b:move(bw + 8, y); b:resize(math.max(10, w - (bw + 8) * 2), PAGE_H - 2) b:setStyleSheet("background-color: #0d1117; border: 0px;") b:echo(string.format("<center><span style='color:%s'>%s</span></center>", self.pages > 1 and "#8a93a8" or "#4a5468", self.total == 0 and "" or ("page " .. self.page .. " of " .. self.pages))) b:show() end
-- setClickCallback passes its extra argument straight through, so the panel -- names itself rather than needing a closure per panel local function page_move(name, delta) local p = P.reg[tostring(name or "")] if not p then return end p.page = (p.page or 1) + delta p:page_paint() end
function P.page_prev(arg) page_move(arg, -1) end function P.page_next(arg) page_move(arg, 1) end
-- Put the view back on the first line. A console follows its own tail as lines -- arrive, which is right for a log and wrong for a document - nobody opens a -- help file to read the last paragraph. Called twice because the buffer is -- still being filled while the trigger that asked for this is running. function Panel:scrolltop() if not (self.console and self.console.name) then return end if not aardkit.util.has("scrollTo") then return end local n = self.console.name pcall(scrollTo, n, 0) tempTimer(0.1, function() pcall(scrollTo, n, 0) end) end
-- copy the line the current trigger fired on, colours intact function Panel:capture_line() if not self.console then return end selectCurrentLine() copy() appendBuffer(self.console.name) end
--- -- registry ---
function P.new(spec) assert(spec and spec.name, "panel needs a name")
local p = setmetatable({}, Panel) -- P.get and the 'panel <name>' command both lower-case what they look up -- (U.split_verb forces it), so a panel registered with any capital was -- addressable by nothing. Normalise once, here. p.name = tostring(spec.name):lower() p.title = spec.title or spec.name p.x = spec.x or "10px" p.y = spec.y or "40px" p.w = spec.width or 460 p.h = spec.height or 220 p.fontSize = spec.fontSize p.wrap = spec.wrap p.consoleless = spec.consoleless -- no background at all; see container_style. Only the map wants this. p.clear = spec.clear p.onbuild = spec.onbuild p.onresize = spec.onresize p.defmode = spec.mode or DEFAULT_MODE
p.transient = spec.transient
p:_build() -- A transient panel holds one thing at a time and is put up by whatever -- produced it - help files, and anything else that arrives rather than -- accumulates. Restoring it visible at login would show an empty frame, or -- last session's leftovers. Geometry still persists; only visibility is -- forced, and the state is set rather than just the widget hidden, or -- visible() would disagree with what's on screen and toggle would need two -- presses. if p.transient then st(p.name).hidden = true end if st(p.name).hidden then p.holder:hide() end
-- Overwriting silently would strand the previous panel's widgets on screen -- with nothing left holding a reference to hide them. local prev = P.reg[p.name] if prev and prev ~= p then U.warn("panel '" .. p.name .. "' registered twice - the earlier one is being replaced") if prev.holder then pcall(function() prev.holder:hide() end) end end P.reg[p.name] = p return p end
--- -- resize -- -- Adjustable.Container raises AdjustableContainerRepositionFinish when you let -- go of a drag, and that is the only notice we get - there is no event while -- the mouse is still down. Anything that lays itself out by hand needs telling, -- or it keeps the geometry from before the drag and its widgets sit where the -- panel used to be. ---
function P.on_reposition(_, name) for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.holder and p.holder.name == name and p.onresize then pcall(p.onresize, p) end end end
U.killhandler(aardkit_panel_resize_handler) aardkit_panel_resize_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler( "AdjustableContainerRepositionFinish", "aardkit.panel.on_reposition")
-- everything of ours, above everything of theirs function P.raiseall() for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p:visible() then p:raise() end end end
function P.get(name) return P.reg[(name or ""):lower()] end
--- -- commands ---
local function list() local rows = {} for name, p in pairs(P.reg) do rows[#rows + 1] = { name, p.mode .. (p:visible() and "" or ", hidden") } end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) if #rows == 0 then U.note("No panels registered.") return end U.help("Panels", rows) end
-- One line per module, rather than every module growing its own copy of this. -- -- A panel belongs to a module, so 'asciimap opacity 200' is where somebody will -- look for it - not 'panel asciimap opacity 200'. Both work; this is what makes -- the first one a single line in the module's dispatcher rather than a -- reimplementation of the second. -- -- Returns true when it handled the verb, so a caller reads: -- if aardkit.panel.verb("chat", verb, rest) then return end function P.verb(name, verb, rest) verb = tostring(verb or ""):lower() if verb ~= "opacity" then return false end P.cmd(name .. " opacity " .. U.trim(tostring(rest or ""))) return true end
function P.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" or verb == "list" then list()
elseif verb == "opacity" then local n = tonumber(U.trim(rest)) if not n or n < 0 or n > 255 then U.warn("Usage: panel opacity <0-255> (currently " .. P.opacity .. "; 255 is solid)") return end P.opacity = math.floor(n) st("_opacity").value = P.opacity save_state() -- every panel that's up, so it takes without a reload. A panel with its -- own setting keeps it: that's what an override is for. local kept = 0 for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if st(p.name).opacity then kept = kept + 1 end p:restyle() end U.ok("Default panel background " .. P.opacity .. "/255" .. (P.opacity < 255 and " - the game will show through." or " - solid.") .. (kept > 0 and (" (" .. kept .. " with their own setting kept it.)") or ""))
-- The stock module reserved these and Mudlet writes them to the profile, so -- they outlived the module that set them: 405px of right column with -- nothing left to draw in it. elseif verb == "scrollbars" or verb == "scrollbar" then local want = U.trim(rest):lower() if want ~= "on" and want ~= "off" then U.help("panel scrollbars", { { "state", P.scrollbars and "on" or "off" }, { "" }, { "Panel consoles scroll with the wheel either way; this is only" }, { "whether a bar takes a column down the right of each one." }, { "" }, { "The main window's own bar is Mudlet's and stays - it is themed" }, { "to match, which is what the stock module used to do app-wide." }, { "" }, { "panel scrollbars on|off", "switch it" }, }) return end P.scrollbars = (want == "on") st("_scrollbars").value = P.scrollbars save_state() local n = 0 for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.console then P.scrollbar(p.console); n = n + 1 end end -- modules with consoles of their own (chat's eight tabs) rebuild theirs raiseEvent("aardkit.panel.scrollbars", P.scrollbars) U.ok("Panel scrollbars " .. want .. " (" .. n .. " console(s))")
elseif verb == "borders" then local want = U.trim(rest):lower() local sides = { "Left", "Right", "Top", "Bottom" } if want == "clear" or want == "reset" then local kept = {} for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.mode == "frame" and st(p.name).framepos then kept[st(p.name).framepos:sub(1,1):upper() .. st(p.name).framepos:sub(2)] = p.name end end local freed = {} for _, side in ipairs(sides) do if not kept[side] and border(side) > 0 then freed[#freed + 1] = side:lower() .. " " .. border(side) .. "px" setborder(side, 0) end end for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.mode == "frame" then p:_build() end end U.ok(#freed > 0 and ("Reclaimed " .. table.concat(freed, ", ") .. ".") or "Nothing to reclaim - no border is reserved that a panel isn't using.") return end local rows = {} for _, side in ipairs(sides) do local owner for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.mode == "frame" and st(p.name).framepos == side:lower() then owner = p.name end end rows[#rows + 1] = { side:lower(), border(side) .. "px" .. (owner and (" " .. owner) or (border(side) > 0 and " nobody - left over" or "")) } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "panel borders clear", "give back every border no panel is using" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Mudlet reserves these out of the console and saves them with" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "the profile, so one set by a module you have since removed" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "stays reserved until something hands it back." } U.help("Main window borders", rows)
elseif verb == "autodock" then local want = U.trim(rest):lower() if want ~= "on" and want ~= "off" then U.help("panel autodock", { { "default", P.autodock and "on - drag one to an edge and it sticks" or "off - docking by command only" }, { "" }, { "Drag a floating dockable window to an edge of the main window" }, { "and Mudlet attaches it there. Off, you lose the gesture and" }, { "nothing else - 'panel <name> dock bottom' still docks." }, { "" }, { "panel autodock on|off", "the default every panel follows" }, { "panel <name> autodock on|off", "override it for one panel" }, { "panel <name> autodock default", "follow the shared setting again" }, }) return end P.autodock = (want == "on") st("_autodock").value = P.autodock save_state() local n = 0 for _, p in pairs(P.reg) do if p.mode == "dock" then n = n + p:apply_autodock() end end U.ok("Drag-to-dock " .. want .. (n > 0 and (" (" .. n .. " window(s) updated)") or ""))
elseif verb == "raise" or verb == "top" then P.raiseall() U.ok("Panels raised above the module's windows.")
elseif verb == "save" then if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.saveAll then Adjustable.Container.saveAll() end save_state() U.ok("Panel layout saved.")
elseif verb == "load" then if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.loadAll then Adjustable.Container.loadAll() end U.ok("Panel layout reloaded.")
elseif verb == "reset" then P.state = {} save_state() U.warn("Panel state cleared - reload the profile to rebuild them.")
elseif verb == "help" or verb == "?" then U.help("panel", { { "panel", "list every panel, its mode and visibility" }, { "panel <name> show", "show it" }, { "panel <name> hide", "hide it" }, { "panel <name> dock", "make it a real dockable window" }, { "panel <name> dock <edge>", "and snap it there: top bottom left right floating" }, { "panel autodock on|off", "drag a dockable panel to an edge to attach it" }, { "panel scrollbars on|off", "whether panel consoles show a scrollbar" }, { "panel borders", "what the main window has reserved, and who is using it" }, { "panel borders clear", "hand back any border no panel is using" }, { "panel <name> autodock on|off", "override that for one panel" }, { "panel <name> embed", "put it back inside the main window" }, { "panel <name> clear", "empty its buffer" }, { "panel <name> reset", "put it back where it started, geometry and all" }, { "panel <name> frame bottom [h]", "in the main window's border, ABOVE the command line" }, { "panel <name> frame off", "out of the border again" }, { "panel raise", "bring every panel above the module's GUI" }, { "panel save", "write the current layout to disk" }, { "panel opacity <0-255>", "the default every panel follows; 255 is solid" }, { "panel <name> opacity <n>", "override it for one panel" }, { "panel <name> opacity default", "follow the shared setting again" }, { "panel load", "reload the saved layout" }, { "panel reset", "forget all panel state" }, { "" }, { "Embedded panels: drag the title bar to move, edges to resize," }, { "right-click for the built-in menu. Docked panels are dragged" }, { "out to float and back onto an edge to dock; Mudlet keeps that." }, })
else local p = P.get(verb) if not p then U.warn("No panel called '" .. verb .. "'. Try 'panel' for the list.") return end local act = U.trim(rest):lower() if act == "" or act == "toggle" then p:toggle() elseif act == "show" then p:show() elseif act == "hide" then p:hide() elseif act == "reset" then p:reset() elseif act:match("^frame") then local a1, a2 = act:match("^frame%s+(%S+)%s*(%S*)") p:setframe(a1 or "bottom", a2 ~= "" and a2 or nil) elseif act:match("^autodock") then local want = U.trim(act:gsub("^autodock", "")) if want == "" then U.help("panel " .. p.name .. " autodock", { { "this panel", st(p.name).autodock ~= nil and ((st(p.name).autodock and "on" or "off") .. " (its own)") or ((P.autodock and "on" or "off") .. " (following the default)") }, { "default", P.autodock and "on" or "off" }, { "" }, { "panel " .. p.name .. " autodock on|off", "set just this one" }, { "panel " .. p.name .. " autodock default", "follow the shared setting again" }, }) elseif want == "default" or want == "clear" or want == "reset" then st(p.name).autodock = nil save_state(); p:apply_autodock() U.ok(p.name .. " follows the default again.") elseif want == "on" or want == "off" then st(p.name).autodock = (want == "on") save_state(); p:apply_autodock() U.ok(p.name .. " drag-to-dock " .. want .. ".") else U.warn("Usage: panel " .. p.name .. " autodock on|off|default") end elseif act == "dock" then p:setmode("dock") elseif act:match("^dock%s+%S+") then p:setdock(act:match("^dock%s+(%S+)")) elseif act == "embed" then p:setmode("embed") elseif act == "clear" then p:clear() elseif act:match("^opacity") then local want = U.trim(act:gsub("^opacity", "")) if want == "" then local own = st(p.name).opacity U.help("panel " .. p.name .. " opacity", { { "this panel", own and (own .. "/255 (its own)") or (P.opacity .. "/255 (following the default)") }, { "default", P.opacity .. "/255" }, { "" }, { "panel " .. p.name .. " opacity <0-255>", "set just this one" }, { "panel " .. p.name .. " opacity default", "follow the shared setting again" }, { "panel opacity <0-255>", "change the shared setting" }, }) elseif want == "default" or want == "clear" or want == "reset" then st(p.name).opacity = nil save_state(); p:restyle() U.ok(p.name .. " follows the default again (" .. P.opacity .. "/255).") else local n = tonumber(want) if not n or n < 0 or n > 255 then U.warn("Usage: panel " .. p.name .. " opacity <0-255> | default") else st(p.name).opacity = math.floor(n) save_state(); p:restyle() U.ok(p.name .. " background " .. math.floor(n) .. "/255, overriding the default.") end end else U.warn("panel " .. verb .. " show|hide|dock [edge]|frame <side>|embed|clear|reset|opacity|autodock") end end end
--- -- lifecycle ---
load_state() scrollbar_style()
-- Mudlet saves UserWindow geometry itself; this covers the embedded ones -- and our mode/visibility bookkeeping. function aardkit.panel.on_exit() if Adjustable and Adjustable.Container and Adjustable.Container.saveAll then pcall(Adjustable.Container.saveAll) end -- drop state for panels nothing registers any more, so retiring a plugin -- doesn't leave its geometry behind forever for name in pairs(P.state) do if not P.reg[name] then P.state[name] = nil end end save_state() end
U.killhandler(aardkit_panel_exit_handler) aardkit_panel_exit_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysExitEvent", "aardkit.panel.on_exit")
-- The AardwolfMudlet GUI assembles itself on a timer after load and lands on -- top of us — that's how a panel ends up buried under the chat tabs. Raising -- once at script time is too early, so do it again once it has settled. function aardkit.panel.on_connect() -- the module's GUI assembles on its own timers and can land on top after -- any one of ours, so try at several points rather than guessing one for _, t in ipairs({ 3, 8, 15, 30 }) do tempTimer(t, P.raiseall) end end
U.killhandler(aardkit_panel_connect_handler) aardkit_panel_connect_handler = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", "aardkit.panel.on_connect")

Script.name: 20_cmd
Script.script:
--[[ aardkit top-level command Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31 ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} local U = aardkit.util.named("Aardkit")
-- plugins register themselves here so 'aardkit' can list what's loaded aardkit.plugins = aardkit.plugins or {}
function aardkit.register(name, desc, cmd) -- Silently replacing would leave the first module registered, loaded, and -- unreachable - its command answering as somebody else's. local prev = aardkit.plugins[name] if prev and prev.cmd ~= cmd then aardkit.util.warn("two modules both registered '" .. tostring(name) .. "' - the later one wins, the earlier is now unreachable") end aardkit.plugins[name] = { desc = desc, cmd = cmd } end
function aardkit.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg)
if verb == "" or verb == "help" or verb == "?" then local rows = { { "aardkit", "this list" }, { "aardkit plugins", "what's loaded" }, { "aardkit stock", "what we switch off in the stock AardwolfMudlet module" }, { "aardkit gmcp", "which GMCP packages we ask for, and which module wants each" }, { "aardkit probe", "which Mudlet functions actually exist here" }, { "aardkit colours", "your ANSI palette against a readable one" }, { "aardkit gaglog on|off", "keep gagged lines in the session log" }, { "panel", "manage the docked/embedded windows" }, } local names = {} for n in pairs(aardkit.plugins) do names[#names + 1] = n end table.sort(names) for _, n in ipairs(names) do rows[#rows + 1] = { n, aardkit.plugins[n].desc } end U.help("aardkit " .. aardkit.version, rows)
-- Aardwolf sends nothing until asked and Mudlet never asks. Worth being able -- to see, because the failure is a panel that just never fills in. elseif verb == "gmcp" then if U.trim(rest):lower() == "redo" then aardkit.gmcp.negotiate() U.ok("Re-sent the GMCP handshake.") return end local rows = aardkit.gmcp.declared() rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } local live = {} for _, k in ipairs({ "char", "comm", "room" }) do live[#live + 1] = k .. (type(gmcp) == "table" and gmcp[k] and " yes" or " -") end rows[#rows + 1] = { "arriving", table.concat(live, " ") }
-- group on its own, because a dash there means something different. -- char/comm/room are primed on connect with 'request'; there is no -- 'request group', so group is only ever sent when the group CHANGES. -- Solo since login and nothing has changed, so nothing has been sent - -- which is indistinguishable from the toggle having failed unless the -- readout says so. local g = type(gmcp) == "table" and gmcp.group rows[#rows + 1] = { "group", g and ("yes - " .. tostring(g.count or 0) .. " member(s)") or "nothing yet; Aardwolf only sends it when a group changes" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit gmcp redo", "ask again now" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Every package Aardwolf offers goes in the list whether or not" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "anything here reads it: Core.Supports.Set REPLACES, so asking" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "for only our own would downgrade whatever else is installed." } U.help("GMCP", rows)
elseif verb == "stock" then if aardkit.stock then aardkit.stock.cmd(rest) else U.warn("stock module handling isn't loaded.") end
-- Mudlet ships the VGA palette, where the *normal* colours are the dark -- half - blue is #000080, navy on a black background, and Aardwolf writes a -- great deal in plain @b. MUSHclient inverts that: saturated normals, pastel -- brights, which is why the same MUD reads darker here than it did there. -- -- Nothing can fix it from in here. The palette lives in the profile's <Host> -- element, and this Mudlet has no setter for it: no setAnsiColor, getAnsiColor -- is read-only, and setConfig's key list has no ANSI colours in it. So the -- most this can do is read what you've got, say whether it's the dark set, -- and hand you the numbers. elseif verb == "colours" or verb == "colors" then -- ansi 0-7 normal, 8-15 bright, in the standard order local NAMES = { [0] = "black", "red", "green", "yellow", "blue", "magenta", "cyan", "white", "light black", "light red", "light green", "light yellow", "light blue", "light magenta", "light cyan", "light white", } -- lifted off the MUSHclient world file this profile was ported from local WANT = { [0] = "#3C3C3C", "#F80000", "#00F800", "#F8F800", "#0000F8", "#F800F8", "#00F8F8", "#FCFCFC", "#BCBCBC", "#FF7878", "#78FF78", "#FFFF78", "#7878FF", "#FF78FF", "#78FFFF", "#FFFFFF", } if not U.has("getAnsiColor") then U.warn("This Mudlet has no getAnsiColor - can't read the palette.") return end local rows, differ = {}, 0 for i = 0, 15 do local ok, r, g, b = pcall(getAnsiColor, i) local cur = ok and r and string.format("#%02X%02X%02X", r, g, b) or "?" local want = WANT[i] local same = (cur:upper() == want:upper()) if not same then differ = differ + 1 end rows[#rows + 1] = { NAMES[i], string.format("<%s>%s<r> %s%s", cur ~= "?" and cur or "#808080", cur, want, same and "" or " <- suggested") } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } if differ == 0 then rows[#rows + 1] = { "Nothing to do - that's the suggested palette already." } else rows[#rows + 1] = { differ .. " of 16 differ. Settings > Preferences > Display," } rows[#rows + 1] = { "the colour swatches. Mudlet has no way to set these from" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "a script, so they have to be typed in once." } end U.help("ANSI palette", rows)
elseif verb == "gaglog" then local v = U.trim(rest):lower() if v == "on" or v == "off" then U.gaglog(v == "on") end U.ok("Gagged lines are " .. (U.gaglog() and "written to the session log behind a marker." or "not logged - what we hide is gone."))
elseif verb == "probe" then -- Mudlet's Lua-side API isn't greppable in the binary, so ask the -- interpreter instead of guessing at it again local rows = {} for _, n in ipairs({ "cecho", "decho", "hecho", "echoLink", "cechoLink", "dechoLink", "tempTimer", "killTimer", "tempRegexTrigger", "tempLineTrigger", "killTrigger", "registerAnonymousEventHandler", "killAnonymousEventHandler", "registerNamedTimer", "deleteNamedTimer", "deleteMap", "clearMap", "addRoom", "addAreaName", "setExit", "addSpecialExit", "setCustomEnvColor", "saveMap", "getRooms", "postHTTP", "getHTTP", "startLogging", "getProfileName", }) do rows[#rows + 1] = { n, type(_G[n]) } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "db", type(db) } rows[#rows + 1] = { "db.create", type(db) == "table" and type(db.create) or "n/a" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Geyser.Gauge", (Geyser and type(Geyser.Gauge)) or "nil" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Adjustable.Container", (Adjustable and type(Adjustable.Container)) or "nil" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "table.save", type(table.save) } U.help("API probe", rows)
elseif verb == "plugins" then local names = {} for n in pairs(aardkit.plugins) do names[#names + 1] = n end table.sort(names) if #names == 0 then U.note("Nothing registered.") else U.note(#names .. " loaded: " .. table.concat(names, ", ")) end
else local p = aardkit.plugins[verb] if p and p.cmd then p.cmd(rest) else U.warn("Unknown: aardkit " .. verb) end end end

Script.name: 30_tags
Script.script:
--[[ Tag gag Sean Stoves, 2026-07-31
'tags on' is what makes everything else here possible — it's how the MUD tells us a spell landed, who's in the room, what's in a shop. It also dumps protocol noise all over the screen.
So: hide the tags, keep the game. Gagging in Mudlet is deleteLine(), which removes the line from the display but not from trigger processing — every plugin still sees the tag it cares about, you just stop looking at it.
Three behaviours, because tags aren't all the same shape:
line a tag that IS the payload {affon}72,1650 -> hide it block a bulk dump between markers {spellheaders}... -> hide all of it marker a wrapper round normal output {roomchars}... -> hide the markers only; the lines between are the room description you actually want to read
Unknown tags default to 'marker' — hide the wrapper, never swallow content. Guessing wrong that way costs you a stray brace; the other way costs you the game text. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.tags = aardkit.tags or {}
local T = aardkit.tags local U = aardkit.util.named("Tags")
