-- the payload IS the tag; nothing to keep local LINE = { affon = true, affoff = true, sfail = true, recon = true, recoff = true, skillgain = true, invitem = true, invmon = true, stat = true, statmon = true, chan = true, tell = true, quest = true, mapstart = true, mapend = true, }
-- Bulk dumps; hide the lot. local BLOCK = { invdata = true, skills = true, }
-- Blocks another plugin parses. We keep our hands entirely off these — not the -- contents, not even the markers. -- -- Removing them from BLOCK wasn't enough: the marker triggers below are generic -- and were still deleting the {/tag} line before the parser could see it, so its -- capture never closed. And the rows got deleteLine()'d twice, which is what -- left blank gaps in the output. One owner per block, all the way through. -- Which of these are corroborated: a sweep of 45 sessions (~90MB) shows only -- rdesc, coords, roomchars, invmon, affon, affoff, invitem, scan, skillgain, -- sfail, recon, recoff, bigmap, spellheaders and recoveries actually arriving. -- The rest - chan, tell, quest, mapstart, mapend, stat, statmon, exits, -- roomname, invdata, skills - are from Aardwolf's tag protocol and are off -- unless you turn them on in-game, so never having seen one is expected rather -- than evidence it isn't real. They stay: a classification that never fires -- costs nothing, and dropping them would break the first person who does enable -- one. Treat the uncorroborated ones as unverified if you change their kind. local OWNED = { spellheaders = true, recoveries = true, coords = true, -- helpwin clears a panel on {help} and copies every line into it until -- {/help}. If the generic marker triggers below also deleted the wrapper, -- both would be calling deleteLine() on the same line - the exact double-gag -- that left blank gaps in the room description. help = true, helpsearch = true, helpkeywords = true, -- Loot Tracker intercepts 'inv', sends invdata and reprints the block, so it -- gags these itself. Left in BLOCK/LINE they were deleted twice - and worse, -- the block gag would have eaten the reply before the parser saw it. invdata = true, invitem = true, }
-- wrappers around text worth reading; hide only the markers local MARKER = { roomchars = true, rdesc = true, exits = true, roomname = true, }
local CFG = U.load("tags", { on = true, extra = {} })
-- anything the user adds by hand for name, how in pairs(CFG.extra or {}) do if how == "line" then LINE[name] = true elseif how == "block" then BLOCK[name] = true else MARKER[name] = true end end
local inblock, block_trig, block_timer = nil, nil, nil
local function kind(name) if LINE[name] then return "line" end if BLOCK[name] then return "block" end return "marker" end
-- A block's contents aren't tagged, so swallowing them needs a catch-all — and a -- PERMANENT catch-all would run Lua on every line the MUD ever sends. Arm one -- only for the length of the block instead, the way Who Poller does its gag. local function close_block() inblock = nil if block_trig then killTrigger(block_trig); block_trig = nil end if block_timer then killTimer(block_timer); block_timer = nil end end
local function open_block(name) close_block() inblock = name -- Everything except the closing marker, which T.on_close owns. Both used to -- fire on '{/name}' and two deletes on one line takes the line after it as -- well - that is where the blank gaps came from. block_trig = tempRegexTrigger("^(?!\\{/).*$", function() U.gag() end) -- if the closing marker never lands, let go rather than eating the session block_timer = tempTimer(6, function() if inblock then close_block() U.warn("Tag gag: {" .. tostring(name) .. "} never closed, released.") end end) end
--- -- triggers ---
-- an opening marker or a self-contained tag: ^{name}rest function T.on_open(name) if not CFG.on then return end name = (name or ""):lower() if OWNED[name] then return end -- its parser gags it U.gag() if kind(name) == "block" then open_block(name) end -- 'line' and 'marker' both just lose this one line end
-- a closing marker: ^{/name} function T.on_close(name) if not CFG.on then return end if OWNED[(name or ""):lower()] then return end U.gag() if inblock and (name or ""):lower() == inblock then close_block() end end
--- -- commands ---
local function listing() local function names(t) local a = {} for k in pairs(t) do a[#a + 1] = k end table.sort(a) return table.concat(a, " ") end U.help("Tag gag", { { "gagging", CFG.on and "on" or "OFF" }, { "" }, { "line (hidden entirely)" }, { " " .. names(LINE) }, { "block (hidden with their contents)" }, { " " .. names(BLOCK) }, { "marker (markers hidden, text kept)" }, { " " .. names(MARKER) }, { "owned (left alone; another plugin parses them)" }, { " " .. names(OWNED) }, { "" }, { "aardtags off", "show the raw tags again" }, { "aardtags line|block|marker <tag>", "classify one yourself" }, { "aardtags forget <tag>", "drop a custom classification" }, { "" }, { "Gagging hides lines from the screen only - every plugin still" }, { "sees them, so nothing stops working." }, }) end
function T.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest):lower()
if verb == "" or verb == "list" or verb == "status" then listing()
elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then CFG.on = (verb == "on") close_block() U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("Tag gag " .. verb .. ".")
elseif verb == "line" or verb == "block" or verb == "marker" then if rest == "" then U.warn("Usage: aardtags " .. verb .. " <tagname>") return end LINE[rest], BLOCK[rest], MARKER[rest] = nil, nil, nil if verb == "line" then LINE[rest] = true elseif verb == "block" then BLOCK[rest] = true else MARKER[rest] = true end CFG.extra[rest] = verb U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("{" .. rest .. "} treated as " .. verb .. ".")
elseif verb == "forget" then if CFG.extra[rest] then CFG.extra[rest] = nil U.save("tags", CFG) U.ok("{" .. rest .. "} back to its default; reload to apply.") else U.warn("No custom rule for {" .. rest .. "}.") end
else listing() end end
aardkit.register("tags", "hide Aardwolf's protocol tags from the screen", T.cmd)

Script.name: 40_stock
Script.script:
--[==[ Standing clear of the stock AardwolfMudlet module Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
A short list of things in aardwolf.xml that actively misbehave, switched off so they stop interfering. Nothing here edits their package - we only disable by name at runtime, so their file is untouched and a reinstall or update of theirs just gets disabled again next load.
Two entries.
The alias 'runto rt':
elseif string.match("the witches of omen tor omentor", matches[2]:lower()) send("run 2s10e2n7e7n11e4n4e;enter hole") --vidblain tempTimer(1,[[aard.coordrun(15578)]])
It swallows every 'runto' and answers a handful of them with speedwalks hardcoded to whoever wrote it, so 'runto omentor' sends someone else's Vidblain route and the MUD answers "Invalid directions in command."
Then it calls aard.coordrun, which is worse:
function aard.coordrun(roomid) if aard.state == 3 and ...areaName... == "vidblain" then display(aard.state) ; gotoRoom(roomid) else display(aard.state) aard.crun = tempTimer(1, function () aard.coordrun(roomid) end) end end
Anywhere but Vidblain that's an infinite loop printing aard.state - a bare "3" every second, forever, with a fresh timer per 'runto' you type. Only the newest is tracked in aard.crun, so the rest run until you reconnect.
Disabling their alias hands 'runto' back to the MUD, which is what it should have been doing.
And the trigger 'cp check', which fires on every "You still have to kill" line - ours included - and the first time each session answers it by sending 'cp info' behind your back. 'cp info' lists every target including the ones you have already killed, so a panel that had just been filled with the 13 you still owe gets replaced by all 15. It also does selectString/replace("") on the line as it goes past, rewriting output we are in the middle of parsing. ]==]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.stock = aardkit.stock or {}
local S = aardkit.stock local U = aardkit.util.named("Stock")
local CFG = U.load("stock", { off = { ["runto rt"] = true }, -- aliases trig = { ["cp check"] = true }, -- triggers script = {}, -- scripts; empty, see below -- The whole module, off. Every package in it - triggers, aliases, scripts, -- keys - is wrapped in one top-level group called 'aard', so four calls -- switch off all of it and four more bring it back. Nothing is deleted. -- -- Off by default, and it has to stay that way: their module is where the -- chat tabs, the gauges, the group panel and the numpad bindings come from, -- and none of those have been rebuilt here yet. See 'aardkit stock all'. all = false, }) CFG.script = CFG.script or {}
-- onRoom is stood down through their own aard.map.enable now, not by name, so -- any leftover entry from an older config is a retry that can only ever fail - -- and it failed loudly, twenty times, in a warning about a stray '3' that has -- nothing to do with it. Drop it wherever it's parked. for _, set in ipairs({ CFG.off, CFG.trig, CFG.script }) do if type(set) == "table" then set.onRoom = nil end end
-- Their whole module lives under one group name per package. local GROUP = "aard" local WHOLE = { { "disableTrigger", "enableTrigger", "triggers" }, { "disableAlias", "enableAlias", "aliases" }, { "disableScript", "enableScript", "scripts" }, { "disableKey", "enableKey", "keys" }, }
-- What you lose with it, said plainly rather than discovered afterwards. Kept -- here so the warning can't drift away from the switch it belongs to. local COSTS = { "chat tabs - All, Private, Group, Tell, Say, Spouse, Clan, Friend", "the gauges along the bottom", "the group panel", "22 numpad bindings - potions, directions, scan, con all, portal", "vconfig, PlayerNotes, startermap, their GUI frame", }
-- why each one is switched off, shown by 'aardkit stock' local WHY = { ["runto rt"] = "hardcodes someone else's speedwalks and leaks a 1/sec timer printing '3'", ["cp check"] = "answers our 'cp check' by sending 'cp info', which lists the targets you have already killed", }
-- disableAlias returns false when there's no alias by that name yet - it does -- not raise - so pcall's flag only ever meant "didn't crash". We were counting -- that as success and saying nothing either way, which is the one outcome this -- file exists to prevent: their runaway timer back, and no hint that the guard -- had failed. Take the real return, and keep retrying until it takes. local tries = 0
-- Their trigger named 'cp check' fires on every "You still have to kill" line -- and, the first time each session, sends 'cp info' behind our backs: -- -- selectString( "You still have to kill ", 1 ) -- replace("") -- if not aard.cpLevel then -- aard.cpLevel = aard.cpLevel or 0 -- send("cp info",false) -- end -- -- 'cp info' lists every target including the ones you have already killed, so -- the panel that had just been filled with the 13 you still owe gets replaced -- by all 15. The replace("") mangles the line on the way past too. -- Tracked by NAME, not per list. -- -- 'aardkit stock off <name>' doesn't know whether the thing is an alias, a -- trigger or a script, so it writes the name into all three lists and lets -- whichever one answers do the work. Two of the three then fail by definition - -- and this used to add a name to `missing` for each failure, so a name that had -- been disabled perfectly well as a trigger was still reported as one it -- couldn't disable. That's the 'couldn't disable map quest cp gq' warning: it -- was disabled, twenty times over, and complained about anyway. -- -- One entry per name, and it survives if ANY of the three took. function S.apply() local n, got, tried = 0, {}, {}
local function attempt(name, fn) tried[name] = true if not U.has(fn) then return end local ok, done = pcall(_G[fn], name) if ok and done ~= false then got[name] = true n = n + 1 end end
for name, want in pairs(CFG.off or {}) do if want then attempt(name, "disableAlias") end end for name, want in pairs(CFG.trig or {}) do if want then attempt(name, "disableTrigger") end end -- Scripts are the heavy switch and nothing is in here by default. Disabling -- one stops everything of theirs that reads what it wrote, which is the -- point when you've replaced it and a foot-gun when you haven't. for name, want in pairs(CFG.script or {}) do if want then attempt(name, "disableScript") end end
local missing = {} for name in pairs(tried) do if not got[name] then missing[#missing + 1] = name end end table.sort(missing)
-- the whole module, if that's been asked for. Last, so the named switches -- above still report honestly on their own. if CFG.all then for _, g in ipairs(WHOLE) do if U.has(g[1]) then pcall(_G[g[1]], GROUP) end end end
tries = tries + 1 if #missing > 0 then -- Their package loads on its own schedule, so a fixed handful of retries -- is a guess about someone else's timing. Keep going for a minute, then -- say so once - but only to someone who actually has their package. No -- 'aard' global means it isn't installed and there was never anything -- here to disable, so shut up about it. if tries < 20 then tempTimer(3, S.apply) elseif tries == 20 and aard ~= nil then U.warn("Stock module: couldn't disable " .. table.concat(missing, ", ") .. " - if you see a stray '3' every second, that's why. 'aardkit stock' to retry.") end end -- their runaway timer, if one is already going. Only the newest is tracked -- on their side, so anything older survives until you reconnect. if aard and aard.crun then pcall(killTimer, aard.crun) aard.crun = nil end return n end
function S.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) rest = U.trim(rest)
if verb == "" or verb == "list" then local rows = {} for _, set in ipairs({ { CFG.off or {}, "alias" }, { CFG.trig or {}, "trigger" }, { CFG.script or {}, "script" } }) do for name, want in pairs(set[1]) do rows[#rows + 1] = { name, set[2] .. ", " .. (want and "disabled" or "left alone") .. (WHY[name] and (" - " .. WHY[name]) or "") } end end table.sort(rows, function(a, b) return a[1] < b[1] end) rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "whole module", CFG.all and "DISABLED" or "running" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock on <alias>", "let the module's alias run again" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock off <alias>", "switch it off again" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock all", "what switching the whole module off costs" } U.help("Stock module", rows)
elseif verb == "all" then local v = rest:lower() if v ~= "on" and v ~= "off" then local rows = { { "whole module", CFG.all and "DISABLED" or "running" }, { "" } } if not aard then rows[#rows + 1] = { "installed", "no - nothing here to switch" } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "What goes with it:" } for _, c in ipairs(COSTS) do rows[#rows + 1] = { "", c } end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "None of those have been rebuilt here yet. The mapping half has -" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "'mapper standalone' switches only that, and leaves the rest running." } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock all off", "disable every trigger, alias, script and key of theirs" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "aardkit stock all on", "put it back" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "Nothing is deleted either way, and it takes a reload to settle." } U.help("The whole stock module", rows) return end CFG.all = (v == "off") U.save("stock", CFG) for _, g in ipairs(WHOLE) do local fn = CFG.all and g[1] or g[2] if U.has(fn) then pcall(_G[fn], GROUP) end end if CFG.all then U.ok("Stock module disabled - all four packages.") U.warn("Gone with it: " .. table.concat(COSTS, "; ") .. ".") U.note("Their scripts already ran this session, so reload to see it properly." .. " 'aardkit stock all on' puts it back.") else U.ok("Stock module enabled again. Reload to be sure it's all running.") end
elseif verb == "on" and rest ~= "" then CFG.off[rest], CFG.trig[rest], CFG.script[rest] = nil, nil, nil U.save("stock", CFG) pcall(enableAlias, rest) pcall(enableTrigger, rest) if U.has("enableScript") then pcall(enableScript, rest) end U.ok("Left '" .. rest .. "' alone. Reload to be sure it's back.")
elseif verb == "off" and rest ~= "" then -- we don't know which kind it is, so switch off whichever answers CFG.off[rest] = true CFG.trig[rest] = true CFG.script[rest] = true U.save("stock", CFG) pcall(disableAlias, rest) pcall(disableTrigger, rest) if U.has("disableScript") then pcall(disableScript, rest) end U.ok("Disabled '" .. rest .. "'.")
else U.warn("aardkit stock [list | on <alias> | off <alias> | all on|off]") end end
-- Their package loads on its own schedule, so once at script time isn't enough: -- an alias they create after us would come back up enabled. S.apply re-arms -- itself now until it actually takes, so this only has to start it. S.apply()
U.killhandler(aardkit_stock_connect) aardkit_stock_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() tries = 0 -- their package can reload on connect; earn the retries again tempTimer(3, S.apply) end)

Script.name: 50_gmcp
Script.script:
--[[ GMCP watcher Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01
One place that listens to Aardwolf's GMCP and hands it out at a rate a human can read.
GMCP does not arrive at a readable pace. char.vitals fires on every tick of every fight, and a module that repaints on each one redraws several times a second - the display visibly shifts while you are trying to read it, which is worse than being a second stale. Every module that wanted GMCP was solving that for itself, badly and differently.
So: events mark their subtree dirty, one timer ticks, and a watcher is called at most once per tick and only when the data it asked about actually changed. Work is bounded no matter how hard the MUD talks.
aardkit.gmcp.watch("statmon", { "char.vitals", "char.maxstats" }, fn) aardkit.gmcp.watch("walk", { "room.info" }, fn, true) -- no waiting aardkit.gmcp.val("char.vitals.hp") -- nil-safe read aardkit.gmcp.num("char.status.level") -- and as a number
The fourth argument opts out of the pacing. Most things are better a second late than jittering, but not everything: arriving in a room ends a speedwalk, and a health potion at 35% is not improved by arriving a second later. Those run on the event, still only when their data changed.
Worth knowing if you came from MUSHclient: the handler there does none of this. It broadcasts every message the moment it lands and offers gmcpdata_at_level() to read it - which is what Mudlet already gives you for free as the gmcp table and the gmcp.x.y events. Pacing was each plugin's own problem there, and this is the part that was actually missing.
Aardwolf's char.* messages are one level deep, which is why the change signature below only walks one level. If that ever stops being true this starts missing nested changes rather than reporting them wrongly - it fails quiet, so check here first if a watcher stops firing. ]]
aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.gmcp = aardkit.gmcp or {}
local G = aardkit.gmcp local U = aardkit.util.named("GMCP")
local CFG = U.load("gmcp", { rate = 1 })
-- name -> { paths = {...}, fn = f, sig = "...", now = bool } G.watchers = G.watchers or {}
-- gmcp path -> true, for the events we've already subscribed to local subscribed = {}
local dirty = true
--- -- reading ---
-- "char.vitals.hp" -> gmcp.char.vitals.hp, without exploding on any missing step function G.val(path) local t = gmcp for part in tostring(path or ""):gmatch("[^%.]+") do if type(t) ~= "table" then return nil end t = t[part] end if t == "" then return nil end return t end
function G.num(path) return tonumber(tostring(G.val(path) or "")) end
-- Aardwolf sends numbers as strings about half the time, so a signature has to -- compare their text rather than their type. -- -- And it has to go all the way down. This stopped at one level, which was true -- of char.* and stopped being true at group: an ARRAY of members, each with its -- own vitals nested under info. A one-level walk signs that as -- "members=table: 0x7f9c...", so whether a watcher ever fires comes down to -- whether Mudlet happens to replace that table or write into the old one - -- and the failure is the quiet kind, a panel that just stops updating. -- -- Depth-capped, because a signature that can recurse forever is worse than one -- that misses something. Five clears group.members[n].info.hp with room over. local function sign(v, depth) if type(v) ~= "table" then return tostring(v) end if depth <= 0 then return "..." end local keys, n = {}, 0 for k in pairs(v) do n = n + 1; keys[n] = k end -- A table can hold number and string keys at once, and comparing those two -- directly raises - out here in a timer, where nothing is catching it. table.sort(keys, function(a, b) return tostring(a) < tostring(b) end) local out = {} for i, k in ipairs(keys) do out[i] = tostring(k) .. "=" .. sign(v[k], depth - 1) end return "{" .. table.concat(out, ",") .. "}" end
local function sig_of(path) return sign(G.val(path), 5) end
--- -- watching ---
local function watcher_sig(w) local out = {} for i, p in ipairs(w.paths) do out[i] = sig_of(p) end return table.concat(out, "|") end
-- A callback can be a function or a dotted name, because Mudlet's own -- registerAnonymousEventHandler takes either and every call site here was -- already written that way. Names resolve at call time, so a module that -- reloads is picked up rather than leaving this holding the old function. local function resolve(fn) if type(fn) == "function" then return fn end local o = _G for part in tostring(fn):gmatch("[^%.]+") do if type(o) ~= "table" then return nil end o = o[part] end return type(o) == "function" and o or nil end
-- fire one watcher if what it watches has changed since last time local function fire(name, w) local s = watcher_sig(w) if s == w.sig then return end w.sig = s local f = resolve(w.fn) if not f then U.err("gmcp watcher " .. tostring(name) .. ": " .. tostring(w.fn) .. " isn't a function") return end local ok, err = pcall(f) if not ok then U.err("gmcp watcher " .. tostring(name) .. ": " .. tostring(err)) end end
function G.mark() dirty = true -- the ones that can't wait for the tick for name, w in pairs(G.watchers) do if w.now then fire(name, w) end end end
local function subscribe(path) -- gmcp.char.vitals arrives as the event "gmcp.char.vitals" local ev = "gmcp." .. path if subscribed[ev] then return end subscribed[ev] = true local g = "aardkit_gmcp_" .. ev:gsub("%.", "_") U.killhandler(_G[g]) _G[g] = registerAnonymousEventHandler(ev, "aardkit.gmcp.mark") end
-- Re-registering the same name replaces it rather than stacking a second one, -- because a module reloads when you rebuild and would otherwise be called twice -- for the rest of the session. function G.watch(name, paths, fn, immediate) if type(paths) == "string" then paths = { paths } end G.watchers[name] = { paths = paths or {}, fn = fn, sig = nil, now = immediate and true or false } for _, p in ipairs(paths or {}) do subscribe(p) end dirty = true end
function G.unwatch(name) G.watchers[name] = nil end
function G.tick() if not dirty then return end dirty = false for name, w in pairs(G.watchers) do if not w.now then fire(name, w) end end end
--- -- negotiation -- -- Aardwolf sends nothing until it is asked, and Mudlet never asks - its -- GMCP.lua is a usage tracker, not a handshake. Every reader in this suite -- worked only because the STOCK module negotiates on connect, which is a poor -- thing to depend on when the stated goal is being able to drop it. Nothing -- here sent a single Core.Supports until now. -- -- Modules declare what they use, rather than one list here going stale: -- -- aardkit.gmcp.need("Group 1", "group on") -- -- Two rules learned from their handshake and the wiki: -- -- Set REPLACES the server's list. Two modules each Setting their own package -- leaves only whichever went last, so the declarations are pooled and sent as -- one Set of the union. -- -- And theirs Sets [Char, Comm, Room] - no Group - from its own connect -- handler, so whoever lands second wins and ours could be wiped. Add cannot -- clobber, so the same union goes again as an Add a few seconds later and the -- result no longer depends on who ran first. -- -- 'group on' is the documented toggle and is independent of Supports, so it -- goes both times too - belt and braces on the one package Aardwolf will not -- send by default. ---
-- pkg -> { module = true }, so 'aardkit gmcp' can say WHO wants each one and a -- package nobody claims any more is visible rather than cargo. G.needs = G.needs or {} G.toggles = G.toggles or {} -- "group on" -> module that asked
-- 'tags on' is core, not a plugin's business - core/30_tags.lua opens by saying -- it is what makes everything else possible, and then nothing ever sent it. -- Every module that reads a tag has been working on the STOCK module's -- handshake, so the first profile without it would have had spellups, invdata, -- statmon and roomchars quietly stop, with no tags arriving even to gag. -- -- Declared here rather than in 30_tags because core files load in numeric order -- and that one runs first: calling into this file from there indexes a nil. G.toggles["tags on"] = "tags"
-- Every package Aardwolf offers, asked for whether or not anything here reads -- it. Set REPLACES the server's list, so a Set naming only what WE read is a -- reduction for whoever else is loaded: install nothing but Gauges and -- "Char 1" alone takes the stock module's chat and mapper with it. Their -- handshake runs once on connect and never comes back, so our own Add cannot -- undo it. -- -- Asking for a package nobody reads costs one message and a table Mudlet fills -- in anyway. Clobbering someone else's costs them their module. local BASELINE = { "Char 1", "Comm 1", "Group 1", "Room 1" }
local function supports_list() local want = {} for _, p in ipairs(BASELINE) do want[p] = true end for p in pairs(G.needs) do want[p] = true end local a = {} for p in pairs(want) do a[#a + 1] = '"' .. p .. '"' end if #a == 0 then return nil end table.sort(a) return "[ " .. table.concat(a, ", ") .. " ]" end
-- Aardwolf sends char.* and room.info when they CHANGE. On a fresh connect -- nothing has changed yet, so a panel that reads them has nothing to draw until -- you move or take a hit. Their guiLoad primes it with these; ours never did, -- which is why the first screen after connect was blank rather than wrong. local PRIME = { "request char", "request room", "request quest" }
local function say_all(verb) local list = supports_list() if not list then return end pcall(sendGMCP, "Core.Supports." .. verb .. " " .. list) for t in pairs(G.toggles) do pcall(sendGMCP, t) end end
local function prime() for _, r in ipairs(PRIME) do pcall(sendGMCP, r) end end
-- Set once, then Add repeatedly. -- -- Add cannot reduce anything, so re-sending it is free, and there are several -- ways to end up short: the stock module Sets [Char, Comm, Room] from its own -- connect handler and drops Group if it lands after us, a module can load late -- and declare a package after the first handshake, and a connect can complete -- before the MUD is ready to be told anything. Once is optimism; the schedule -- is what makes "re-add everything" true. local RETRIES = { 3, 8, 20 }
-- Deferred until you are actually in the game, not dropped. -- -- This used to be `if not U.playing() then return end`, and both callers land -- at the login prompt: the need() debounce a second after the scripts load, and -- the connect hook two seconds after the socket opens. On a cold connect the -- handshake therefore never ran at all. It has been working purely because the -- STOCK module negotiates off its own 'Welcome to Aardwolf' trigger - so the -- first clean profile would have come up with no Comm, no Group, no tags and -- nothing primed, and no error to say why. -- -- U.ready queues until gmcp.char.status says state 3, which is the same reason -- the guard was there: a command sent at the password prompt IS the password. function G.negotiate() U.ready(function() -- Stock sends this on every login and it is stored nowhere, so a fresh -- profile talks to Aardwolf in the wrong encoding until something says -- otherwise. pcall(setServerEncoding, "UTF-8") say_all("Set") prime() for _, t in ipairs(RETRIES) do tempTimer(t, function() if U.playing() then say_all("Add") end end) end end) end
-- Debounced: every module calls this at load, and one handshake for the lot -- beats one per module. local pending_neg = false
function G.need(module, pkg, toggle) module = tostring(module or "?") if pkg then G.needs[tostring(pkg)] = G.needs[tostring(pkg)] or {} G.needs[tostring(pkg)][module] = true end if toggle then G.toggles[tostring(toggle)] = module end if pending_neg then return end pending_neg = true tempTimer(1, function() pending_neg = false; G.negotiate() end) end
-- what we ask for, and who asked function G.declared() local rows = {} local want = {} for _, p in ipairs(BASELINE) do want[p] = "" end for p, who in pairs(G.needs) do local names = {} for m in pairs(who) do names[#names + 1] = m end table.sort(names) want[p] = table.concat(names, " ") end local keys = {} for p in pairs(want) do keys[#keys + 1] = p end table.sort(keys) for _, p in ipairs(keys) do rows[#rows + 1] = { p, want[p] ~= "" and want[p] or "baseline - nothing here reads it" } end return rows end
U.every("gmcp", CFG.rate, G.tick)
-- A reconnect brings a fresh char.*; forget what we last saw so every watcher -- fires once on the new data rather than deciding nothing changed. U.killhandler(aardkit_gmcp_connect) aardkit_gmcp_connect = registerAnonymousEventHandler("sysConnectionEvent", function() for _, w in pairs(G.watchers) do w.sig = nil end dirty = true -- The handshake is per-connection, not per-load. Late enough that the MUD -- has finished its own greeting. tempTimer(2, G.negotiate) end)
